**וְיָשֻׁבוּ וְיַחֲנוּ לִפְנֵי פִּי הַחִירוֹת.** עִנְיַן כֹּחַ הַטּוּמְאָה שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַזֹּאת הִיא קְלִיפַּת זְנוּת וְהָיְתָה דְּמוּת זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, וְעַל כֵּן קָרְאוּ שְׁמָהּ פִּי הַחִירוֹת, כִּי אֵצֶל הָאוּמּוֹת נִרְאֶה שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל תַּאֲוֹת לִבּוֹ שָׁם הוּא בֶּן חוֹרִין, עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר "וְיֹאמַר פַּרְעֹה נְבוּכִים הֵם בָּאָרֶץ" כוּ'. הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיַּגִּיעוּ לִפְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַלֵּזוּ יִהְיֶה נִרְאֶה שֶׁהֵם מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם מוּגְדָּרִים מְאֹד בְּזֹאת הַתַּאֲוָה. אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ שֶׁהֵם מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים לְזֶה הַדָּבָר, שֶׁהֲרֵי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין לִבָּם בִּרְשׁוּתָם אֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׂכֶל יִמְשׁוֹל עֲלֵיהֶם, וְרַק תַּאֲוָתָם מוֹשֶׁלֶת עֲלֵיהֶם אֵין לְךָ שִׁעְבּוּד גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.


*“… that they turn back and encamp before Pi Hahirot ….”* (Shemot, 14:2)
The impure power of this form of idolatry was the *kelipah*¹⁶ of *z’nut*, or licentiousness, and as such this particular idol in the desert was in the form of a male and female.¹⁷ Therefore its name was *Pi Hahirot*,¹⁸, the mouth of liberty. for the nations define freedom as the freedom to extend into and perform all the lusts of the heart. On this Pharaoh said, “they are confounded in the land.” As if to say that when they reach this idol it they will be confounded by the realization that they are so enslaved to their physical desires that they go to great lengths to guard themselves with all of the “fences” or extra stringencies of the Torah. In fact the opposite is true, for the nations are enslaved to their lust as their intelligence is not in control of their hearts. Rather they are ruled by their desires, and there is no enslavement greater than this.

footnotes:
¹⁶ Evil force, or “shell.”
¹⁷ Apparently engaged in the act of fornication.
¹⁸ Like pi haheiroot


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/5)


**נִכְחוֹ תַחֲנוּ עַל הַיָּם.** הִנֵּה כָּתוּב (ברכות ס"ג.) "בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" וַאֲפִילּוּ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה. וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן "נִכְחוֹ תַחֲנוּ עַל הַיָּם", הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁאַתֶּם עוֹשִׂים מַעֲשִׂים כְּמוֹ הַמִּצְרִיִּים מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַעֲשֵׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם טוֹבִים, דְּהִנֵּה אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית אֲשֶׁר הֵם חֵלֶק הַש"י הֵם דְּבוּקִים בְּחַיִּים פְּשׁוּטִים בְּלִי שׁוּם לְבוּשׁ וְיוֹנְקִים מִמְּקוֹר חַיִּים הַהוּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהַש"י מוּפְשָׁט מִכָּל מִדּוֹת וּמִכָּל גָּוֶן, רַק פָּשׁוּט בְּתַכְלִית הַפְּשִׁיטוּת, כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בִּמְקוֹר חַיּוּתָם אֵין אֲחִיזָתָם בְּשׁוּם גָּוֶן וּלְבוּשׁ וְכֹחַ, הֵן בְּחָכְמָה, הֵן בְּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת אוֹ בַּעֲשִׁירוּת, בִּלְתִּי בַּה' לְבַדּוֹ. אֲבָל הָאוּמּוֹת יֵשׁ לָהֶם לְכָל אוּמָּה וְאוּמָּה אֵיזֶה כֹּחַ וְגָוֶן אַחֵר, אֲשֶׁר מִזֶּה יִמָּשֵׁךְ כֹּחַ חִיּוּתָם וּבָזֶה הֵם נֶאֱחָזִים. כְּגוֹן בָּבֶל כֹּחָם הוּא בְּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת, וּפְלִשְׁתִּים כֹּחָם בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם יְבַקֵּשׁ תַּחְבּוּלָה עַד אֲשֶׁר יִמְצָא סִיבָּה לְפַרְנָסָה, אוֹ חָכְמָה יְדוּעָה אוֹ מְלָאכָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בָּטוּחַ לִבּוֹ כִּי יִהְיֶה לוֹ בַּמֶּה לְהִתְכַּלְכֵּל. וְעִנְיַן מוֹאָב וּקְלִיפָּתָם הוּא תַּקּוּפוּת, שֶׁהוּא חָזָק בְּדַעְתּוֹ מִכֹּחַ אֲכִילוֹת, וּשְׁאָר דְּבָרִים כָּאֵלֶּה הַמַּחֲזִיקִים וּמַרְחִיבִים הַדַּעַת, וְזֶה עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ כְּמוֹשׁ, הַיְינוּ תַּבְנִית אָדָם נִכְמָשׁ מִמַּרְאֵה יַלְדוּתוֹ, כִּי מִזֶּה הֵם יְרֵאִים פֶּן יִנָּטֵל מֵהֶם אֶת זֹאת הַהַרְחָבָה כְּאָדָם לְעֵת זִקְנָתוֹ שֶׁתַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָתוֹ מִתְמַעֶטֶת וְאֵין הַרְחָבָה בְּדַעְתּוֹ. וְכֵן שְׁאָר הָאוּמּוֹת כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי דַּרְכּוֹ. וְהִנֵּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פִּיזֵּר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבֵין הָאוּמּוֹת, וְהוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בֵּין הַכֹּחוֹת הָהֵם, וְהֵם יִתְבָּרְרוּ וְיִצָּרְפוּ וְיִתְלַבְּנוּ בְּאֵלּוּ הַכֹּחוֹת וְלֹא יִפְנוּ אֲלֵיהֶם וְרַק בַּה' יָשִׂימוּ בִּטְחוֹנָם. וְלֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁהַש"י יִגְאַל אוֹתָם אָז יִתֵּן לָהֶם כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁבֵּרְרוּ עַצְמָם בָּהֶם, וְהַיְינוּ הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת שֶׁל בָּבֶל, וְטוֹבַת עֲשִׁירוּת שֶׁנִּמְצָא בִּפְלִשְׁתִּים, וְהַהַרְחָבָה שֶׁל מוֹאָב, וְכֵן כֻּלָּם יִתֵּן לָהֶם בַּעֲבוּר הַצַּעַר שֶׁסָּבְלוּ מֵהַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ לָהֶם בַּגָּלוּת. אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יִטַּע הַש"י אֵלּוּ הַטּוֹבוֹת בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָז יִהְיוּ מְלֵאִים קְדוּשָּׁה וְגַם יִהְיוּ בְּלִי גְּבוּל שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיוּ מֵהַש"י, כִּי בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת הֵם בְּשִׁיעוּר וְקִצְבָה, אֲבָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיוּ בְּהַשְׁגָּחוֹת הַש"י מִמֵּילָא יִהְיוּ בְּלִי גְּבוּל מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַש"י הוּא בִּלְתִּי גְּבוּל. וְעַל עִנְיַן הַזֶּה מְבוֹאָר בִּנְבוּאַת יְשַׁעְיָה כְּשֶׁנִּבָּא עַל מַפֶּלֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּים נֶאֱמַר "וְרָעוּ בְּכוֹרֵי דַלִּים וְאֶבְיוֹנִים לָבֶטַח יִרְבָּצוּ וְהֵמַתִּי בָרָעָב שָׁרְשֵׁךְ" (ישעיה י"ד,ל') הַיְינוּ מִדָּה בְּמִדָּה מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם אוֹמְרִים שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר אַחַר סִיבָּה לְפַרְנָסָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּטוּחַ עַל חַיָּיו, עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר "וְהֵמַתִּי בָרָעָב שָׁרְשֵׁךְ", וּכְשֶׁהֵם נוֹפְלִים אָז יַכְנִיס הַש"י אֶת כֹּחָם וְטוֹבָתָם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהָיוּ בֵּינֵיהֶם בַּגָּלוּת וְנִבְחֲנוּ בַּמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת, וְהֵם לֹא שָׂמוּ בִּטְחוֹנָם לָזֶה רַק בְּהַש"י, עַל כֵּן "וְרָעוּ בְּכוֹרֵי דַלִּים" הַיְינוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם דַּלִּים וְסוֹמְכִים עַצְמָם עַל הַש"י וְעַכְשָׁיו בְּמַפַּלְתָּם הֵם יִרְעוּ וְיִתְפַּרְנְסוּ. וְכָעִנְיַן הַזֶּה נֶאֱמַר גַּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת שְׁאָר אוּמּוֹת. וְזֶה בֵּיאֵר הַכָּתוּב "נִכְחוֹ תַחֲנוּ עַל הַיָּם" כִּי נִמְנוּ בְּכָאן אַרְבָּעָה כֹּחוֹת וּקְלִיפּוֹת שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם, וְהֵם מִגְדּוֹל וְיָם וּבַעַל צְפוֹן וּפִי הַחִירוֹת. וְאֵלּוּ הָאַרְבָּעָה הֵם עִיקַּר הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם, וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַכָּתוּב "נִכְחוֹ תַחֲנוּ", הַיְינוּ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ וְכַדּוֹמֶה לָהֶם בְּכֹחוֹתָם יִהְיֶה גַּם לָכֶם כָּל הַהֲנָאוֹת וְטוֹבוֹת שֶׁנִּמְצָא לְמִצְרַיִם, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן תִּגָּאֲלוּ מֵהֶם וְיִפְּלוּ לִפְנֵיכֶם, כִּי כָל אֵלּוּ הַכֹּחוֹת אֲשֶׁר בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מְלֵאִים קְדוּשָּׁה אַף שֶׁהֵם דּוֹמִים לְמִצְרַיִם, כִּי "גַּם אֶת זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹקִים" כִּי גַּם כָּאן הָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ, אַךְ שֶׁהַש"י מֵעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁאֵין בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק אַהֲבַת הַש"י.


*“… over against it shall you encamp by the sea.”* (Shemot, 14:2)
It is written (Gemara *Berachot*, 63a), “Know Him in all your ways, even concerning a sin.” Such is the case with “over against it [the idol of *ba’al tsafon*] shall you encamp by the sea.” Even if your actions are similar to the Egyptians, yet still, the actions of Israel are good, for the people of Israel, the portion of God, are cleaving in simple life without any separation and drawing their energy from the Source of life. Just as God is disencumbered of any attribute or any external coloring, but rather exists in absolute simplicity, so too Israel at the source of its life, free of any external force, separation, or subordinate power. Whether concerning wisdom, status, or wealth, Israel is disencumbered of any influence other than God. With the nations, however, each particular nation has its own power and hue from which it draws its life force and to which it grasps hold of.
For example, the power of Babylon was in its status, and the power of the Philistines was in the tricks and wisdom they used to attain wealth, or a crafts with which they could earn a livelihood. The power of Moab and its *kelipah* was strength, strengthening their minds with a healthy diet and the like. Their particular form of idolatry was *Chemosh* (meaning “dried”), meaning the form of a man dried up from its childhood form.¹⁹ Their fear was that this power would be taken away, like an old, senile man with little appetite.
Now God dispersed Israel among the nations so they would be among these powers, to clarify, refine, and clean themselves concerning them, not turning to them but rather placing their trust in God. And in the future, when God will redeem them, He will then give them all the powers from which they had refined themselves, the status of Babylon, the wealth of the Philistines, the strength and mental fortitude of Moab. He shall give them all of these in recompense for all the trials and tribulations they incurred in the exile. Thus when God shall plant these good things among Israel these attributes will be filled with *Kedusha* (holiness) and among Israel they will be limitless since they come from God. Among the nations of the world these good things are given in in a limited way, but with Israel they will come from God’s providence and without limit, as God is without limit.
This is explained in the prophecy of Yesahyahu concerning the fall of the Philistines, saying, “and the firstborn of the poor I shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety, and I will kill your root with famine” (Yesahyahu, 14:30). They will be paid back measure for measure. Since they say that they need to run after sources of livelihood for security (yet security based on a subordinate earthly power), therefore it is said, “and I have killed your root with famine.” Then when they fall, their power and abundance will be brought into Israel. This is because Israel was in exile among them and tested concerning this attribute, not placing their trust in the subordinate power but rather in God. Therefore, “the firstborn of the poor I shall feed,” meaning Israel who are poor and relying on God. Now with the fall of the wealthy Philistines, the poor of Israel will be fed and supported.
It will be similarly so with the downfall of all the other nations. This is the explanation of the verse, “over against it shall you encamp by the sea.” Four powers are enumerated here which are the *kelipot* of Egypt, *migdol* (tower), *yam* (sea), *ba’al tsafon* (master of the north), and *pi haheirot* (the mouth of freedom). Therefore the verse says, “over against it shall you encamp.” Corresponding to them and similar to their powers so will all the benefits and abundance of Egypt be yours, and nevertheless you will be redeemed from them and they will fall before you. When all of these powers are among Israel they are filled with *Kedusha* even if they seem similar to Egypt, for “E-lohim made them one over against the other [everything in *Kedusha* has its “evil twin” in impurity].” The accuser saw them at the Red Sea and claimed, “what is the difference between these and these? [for they both served idols],” yet God testified for them that there is nothing in the hearts of Israel except the love of God.

footnotes:
¹⁹ Perhaps a kind of “shrunken head.”


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/6)


**וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאִים בְּיָד רָמָה.** תַּרְגּוּמוֹ בְּרֵישׁ גְּלֵי הַיְינוּ לֹא בְּיָד רָמָה נֶגֶד אֲחֵרִים בְּגַאֲוָה וְגֵיאוּת רַק שֶׁהֵם בְּנֵי חוֹרִין בְּלִי יִרְאָה וָפַחַד מִשּׁוּם אָדָם.


*“… and the children of Israel left with a high hand.”* (Shemot, 14:8)
The Aramaic translation reads, “with an uncovered head,” meaning not with high hand against others, but rather with pride and confidence, since they are now free and fear no one.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/7)


**ה' יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִשׁוּן.** הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה שֶׁכָּאן נִצְטַוּוּ לְהַחֲרִישׁ מִבְּלִי שׁוּם פְּעֻלָּה וְאַף בִּתְפִלָּה לֹא יִתְפַּלְּלוּ לְהַש"י, וּבְמִלְחֲמוֹת עֲמָלֵק נִמְצָא לְהֵפֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים" וְכוּ', וְנֶאֱמַר "וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה" וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן וַהֲוָה יְדוֹהִי פְּרִישָׂן בִּצְלוֹ. אַךְ הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי יֵשׁ חִלּוּק בֵּין עֲמָלֵק לִשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת, כִּי שְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת אוֹמְרִים שֶׁאֵין הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם וְתוֹלִין כָּל הַשְׁפָּעוֹת טוֹבָה בְּכֹחוֹתָם לֵאמֹר "כֹּחִי וְעֹצֶם יָדִי", וְלָכֵן בְּמִלְחֲמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד מִצְרַיִם נִצְטַוּוּ לְהַחֲרִישׁ, הַיְינוּ לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם וּבָזֶה הָיוּ מְנַצְּחִים, כִּי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְצָא זֹאת הַמְּבִינוּת כִּי הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, וְגַם תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהָאָדָם מִתְפַּלֵּל גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בִּלְתִּי רְצוֹן הַש"י וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר "וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן". אֲבָל בַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר כִּדְאִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין [י"ח.] וְהוּא תּוֹלֶה כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו בְּהַש"י שֶׁאוֹמֵר כָּל הָרַע שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה הוּא בִּרְצוֹן הַש"י, כִּי בְּלֹא רְצוֹן הַש"ילֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת, וְנֶגְדּוֹ הוּא הָעֵצָה לְהַרְאוֹת כִּי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם הוּא בִּידֵי הָאָדָם וְהָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לַעֲבוֹדָה וּתְפִלָּה, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בַּגְּמָרָא (סנהדרין ס'.) עַל רַבְשָׁקֵה שֶׁהָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמַר "הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵי ה' עָשִׂיתִי", וְתָלָה מַעֲשָׂיו הָרָעִים בְּהַש"י וְנֶגְדּוֹ הִיא הָעֵצָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל.


*“God will fight for you, and you shall be silent.”* (Shemot, 14:14)
Concerning this they were commanded to hold their peace and refrain from action, not even praying to God. With the war against Amalek we find the opposite, where it is said, “and it was, when Moshe lifted his hands [they succeeded],” and it said, “and his hands were *emunah*, steady [faithful],” where the Aramaic translation reads, “his hands were spread out in prayer.” There is a difference between Amalek and other nations. Other nations say that not all is in the hands of Heaven, and ascribe all good influence to their own efforts, saying, “my strength and the power of my hands has gotten me this wealth.” Therefore in Israel’s war with Egypt they were commanded to hold their peace, meaning to show that all is in the hands of Heaven, and even the prayer that a man offers cannot be done independent of God’s will. Thus it is said, “and you will be silent.”
The Gemara in *Kedushin* (18a) calls Amalek, “the apostate of Israel.” He ascribes all of his actions to God. He believes that all of his evil is God’s will, as he could not do anything but for the will of the Blessed One. The advice against this belief is to show how man has the power to choose the fear of Heaven, and for this he needs Divine service and prayer. On this the Gemara (*Sanhedrin*, 60a) mentions Ravshakei, an apostate of Israel (see 2 Kings, Ch. 18), who said, “have I come up to this place without God to destroy it!?” In this way he attributes his wickedness to God, and the advice against this is to pray.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ Though it must be investigated, for it says there in verse 36, “and the people held their peace … for the king’s commandment was, answer him not,” which seems like the response for Egypt.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/8)


**וַיּוֹשַׁע ה' בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כוּ'.** הַיְינוּ כִּי אַחֲרֵי יְשׁוּעוֹת גְּאֻלַּת מִצְרַיִם הָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְצִמְצוּם כִּי בִּימֵי הַפֶּסַח יֵשׁ צִמְצוּם בַּאֲכִילָה, כִּי מַצָּה רוֹמֵז עַל זֶה לֶחֶם עֹנִי, וְכָאן אַחַר שֶׁזָּכוּ בְּיוֹם ז' שֶׁל פֶּסַח לִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף נֶאֱמַר "וַיּוֹשַׁע ה'" כוּ', שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ צְרִיכִים עוֹד בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לִגְדָרִים וּסְיָגִים, וְזֶה הָרֶמֶז שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בְּמִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה (דברים ט"ז,ח') "שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים" וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר שִׁבְעַת.


*“Thus God saved Israel on that day ….”* (Shemot, 14:30)
After the great salvation of the redemption from Egypt they needed to experience *tsimtsum* (constriction). During Passover eating is constricted, hinted at in the *matsah*, “the bread of poverty.” But here (in this verse) after they merited the splitting of the Red Sea on the seventh day of Passover, it says, “thus God saved,” etc. On that day they no longer needed “fences” (for the law) and restrictions, and this is hinted at in what is written in the Mishne Torah (meaning the book of *Devarim*, 16:8), “six days,” and it does not say seven.²¹ was only for six days, and then on the seventh, “thus God saved,” meaning releasing them from restrictions and bringing them great salvations.

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/9)


**סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם.** "סוּס" מוֹרֶה עַל מְהִירוּת וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, "וְרוֹכְבוֹ" מוֹרֶה עַל יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת שֶׁמְּצַמְצֵם אֶת הַסּוּס שֶׁלֹּא יָרוּץ. וְהִנֵּה אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּעֵת שֶׁרוֹאִים חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אֵין לָהֶם כֹּחַ לְצַמְצֵם אֶת עַצְמָם רַק מִתְפַּשְּׁטִים בְּכָל תַּאֲוַת לִבָּם, עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר קוֹדֶם "סוּס" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "רוֹכְבוֹ", שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁמְּמַלְּאִים כָּל תַּאֲוָתָם וְאֵין לָהֶם כֹּחַ לְיוֹתֵר, אָז יֶחְדְּלוּ עֲשׂוֹת. אֲבָל בְּהַש"י נֶאֱמַר (חבקוק ג',ח') "כִּי תִרְכַּב עַל סוּסֶיךָ" כוּ'. וְנֶאֱמַר תְּחִלָּה "תִּרְכַּב" הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהַש"י יִתֵּן טוֹבָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּבוֹא לְיַד הָאָדָם, יְצַמְצֵם אוֹתָהּ, שֶׁלֹּא יִקַּח עַד שֶׁיִּרְאֶה אֶת הַנּוֹתֵן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתֵּן אוֹתָהּ בִּכְדֵי שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יוּכַל לְקַחְתָּהּ בְּכָל רְצוֹן לִבּוֹ. עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר קוֹדֶם "כִּי תִרְכַּב" הַמּוֹרֶה עַל חֶשְׁבּוֹן וְיִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ "סוּסֶיךָ" לְשׁוֹן הַשְׁפָּעַת טוֹבָה בִּמְהִירוּת.


*“… horse and its rider He threw into the sea.”* (Shemot, 15:1)
“Horse” teaches of speed and expansion. “Rider” teaches of a settled mind that restrains the horse from running. With the nations see the pleasures of this world, they do not have the power to restrain themselves but rather expand into their desires. Therefore concerning them it says first “horse” and then “rider,” for after they have been filled with all their desires they have no power for more and cease. Yet with God it says (Habakuk, 3:8), “when *you* ride upon your horses and chariots of salvation.” The verse says first “You ride,” to say that when God gives goodness to Israel He constricts it before it comes into their possession, and they do not take it until they fears the giver. Then He gives it in a way that it is received by a fully willing heart. This is why it says first “when You ride,” teaching of reckoning and a settled mind, and after “Your horses,” denoting the effusion of good with great velocity.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/10)


**ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה ה' שְׁמוֹ.** אִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר [רבה פרשה ו',ג'] רְשָׁעִים קוֹדְמִין לִשְׁמָן, "נָבָל שְׁמוֹ", "שֶׁבַע בֶּן בִּכְרִי שְׁמוֹ" אֲבָל הַצַּדִּיקִים שְׁמָן קוֹדֵם לָהֶם, "שְׁמוֹ מָנוֹחַ" "שְׁמוֹ קִישׁ" וכו' "וּשְׁמוֹ מָרְדֳּכַי", לְפִי שֶׁדּוֹמִין לְבוֹרְאָן דִּכְתִיב "וּשְׁמִי ה' לֹא נוֹדַעְתִּי" כוּ'. וְהָעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כָּאן "ה' שְׁמוֹ", דְּהִנֵּה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁשְּׁמָן קוֹדֵם לָהֶן, הוּא כִּי הֵם שׁוֹלְטִין עַל לִבָּם כִּי לִבָּן בִּרְשׁוּתָן כִּי שְׁמוֹ מוֹרֶה עַל רָצוֹן, וְגַם הוּא בְּגִמַטְרִיָּא רָצוֹן כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בראשית רבה פרשה ל"ד,י"א), וְהוּא שֶׁהַצַּדִּיקִים שׁוֹלְטִים עַל רְצוֹנָם מַה שֶּׁיִּפֹּל בְּדַעְתָּם תְּחִלָּה, יִתְיַשְּׁבוּ אַחַר כָּךְ וּבְאִם אֵין נָכוֹן לִפְנֵיהֶם לֹא יַעֲשׂוּ, וּרְשָׁעִים הֵם הֵיפֶךְ כִּי הֵן בִּרְשׁוּת לִבָּן, וְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (ילקוט בשלח רמ"א בשם מדרש אבכיר) כִּי הַשַּׂר שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם בָּא לְהַמְלִיץ עַל מִצְרַיִם שֶׁיְּרַחֵם הַש"י עֲלֵיהֶם, בָּא גַּבְרִיאֵל וְנָטַל לְבֵנָה וְהִנִּיחַ לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהֶרְאָה לְפָנָיו שֶׁבָּזֶה שִׁעְבְּדוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהוּא כִּי בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁהָיוּ מִצְרַיִם רָעִים וְחַטָּאִים הָיָה עוֹד לְלַמֵּד אֵיזֶה זְכוּת עֲלֵיהֶם, כִּי הָיָה נִמְצָא בְּלִבָּם נְטוּיָה לְטוֹבָה קְצָת גַּם כֵּן, וְלָכֵן גַּם הַש"י יִנְהַג עִמָּם בְּרַחְמָנוּת וְיַשְׁגִּיחַ קְצָת לְטוֹבָה, אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא גַּבְרִיאֵל וְהֶרְאָה הַלְּבֵנָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁבָּרִשְׁעוּת הַזֹּאת שֶׁשִּׁעְבְּדוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא הָיָה בְּלִבָּם שׁוּם נְטוּיָה לְטוֹבָה. עַל כֵּן אָמַר הַש"י "ה' שְׁמוֹ", הַיְינוּ מִדָּה בְמִדָּה כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שְׁלִיטָה עַל לִבָּם כָּךְ הַש"י לֹא יְשַׁנֶּה רְצוֹנוֹ מִמִּדַּת הַדִּין, וְזֶהוּ "ה' שְׁמוֹ".


*“God is a man of war, God is His name.”* (Shemot, 15:3)
It is written in Midrash Esther (Rabba, 6:3), “With the wicked, their personal name precedes, ‘is their name,’ such as ‘Naval is his name,’ ‘Sheva ben Bichri is his name,’ and so forth. Yet with the *tsaddikim*, ‘their name is’ precedes their personal name, such as ‘his name is Manoach,’ ‘his name is Kish,’ ‘his name is Mordechai.’ This is because they resemble their Creator, of whom it was said, ‘and My name YHVH I did not make known to them’ (*Shemot*, 6:3).” So here in the Song of the Sea it say, “God is His name,” just as we find with the *tsaddikim*, where “his name is” precedes their personal name, because they control their hearts and their hearts are in their possession. The expression “his name” teaches of will, for even *shmo*, “his name,” is numerically equivalent to “*ratson*,” “will” (both equal 346) as is mentioned in the Midrash (*Bereshit* Rabba, 34:11). The *tsaddikim* control their wills and consider their thoughts. If they deem them improper they refrain. With the wicked it is the opposite as their hearts possess them.
It is written in the Midrash (*Yalkut B’shalach* 241 in the name of the Midrash Avchir), “the angel of Egypt came to recommend that God be merciful with them, so the angel Gavriel came with a brick, placed it before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said, ‘with this Egypt has subjected Israel to slave labor.’ ” With all of Egypt’s sins and wickedness there was still a little room to teach of their merits as their hearts were somewhat inclined towardss the good. Therefore would have been proper for God to be merciful with them and see to their welfare. But when Gavriel came and showed them the brick,²² he was saying that they enslaved Israel with such wickedness that any tendency towardss the good was null. Therefore God said, “God is His name,” meaning that He will deal with them measure for measure, for just as they had no control over their hearts, so too God will not change His will from the attribute of stern justice, and this is “God is His name.”

footnotes:
²² Remember the horror that the Egyptians would make bricks out of Jewish children.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/11)


**מִי כָמוֹךָ בָּאֵלִם ה' מִי כָּמֹכָה נֶאְדָּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ כוּ'.** "מִי כָמוֹךָ בָּאֵלִים", הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא נֶעְלָם מֵעֵין כָּל חַי וְאֵין אֶחָד שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגֵהוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בַּגְּמָרָא (גיטין נ"ו:) "מִי כָּמוֹךָ בָּאִלְּמִים", וְ"נֶאְדָּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ" הַיְינוּ מְפֹרָשׁ כִּי עַל כָּל דָּבָר יוּכַּר מְפֹרָשׁ מְאֹד כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹרֵא, כִּי מִכָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים יִתְרָאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא, כִּי עַל כָּל דָּבָר בָּא בְּלֵב אָדָם הַמְבַקֵּשׁ ה' לֵאמֹר "מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה". וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "הָאַדֶּרֶת וְהָאֱמוּנָה לְחַי הָעוֹלָמִים", אַדִּיר הַיְינוּ מְפֹרָשׁ וֶאֱמוּנָה הַיְינוּ בְּהֶעְלֵם וְהֶסְתֵּר, כִּי הַדָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם אֵין צָרִיךְ אֱמוּנָה, רַק הַדָּבָר שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶסְתֵּר זֶה צָרִיךְ אֱמוּנָה, וְהוּא כִּי לְעֵינֵי אָדָם אֵינוֹ מְפֹרָשׁ רַק הַפְּלִיאָה מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה, וְאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם הַיְינוּ הַהֶעְלֵם וְהַגִּלּוּי אֵינָם מִתְאַחֲדִים רַק בְּהַש"י לְבַדּוֹ.


*“Who is like You among the powers [*eileem*] Hashem? Who is like You, glorious [*ne’edar*] in holiness ….”* (Shemot, 15:11)
“Who is like You among the powers,” is saying that in God’s essence He is hidden from the eye of all life and no one can apprehend Him, as it is explained in the Gemara (*Gittin*, 56b), “who is like You among the speechless.”²³, speechless, signifying unfathomable inwardness. “Glorious in holiness,” is to say, openly revealed, for the Creator is readily apparent in the creation. All created beings are evidence of the Creator, for whatever the seeker of God encounters his heart wells up and he asks, “who created these?” This is the meaning of the phrase in the liturgical poem, “*ha’ederet ve’ha’emuna*,” “the glory and the faith, to the Life of all worlds [God].” “Glorious” means revealed and “faith” means hidden and concealed. Something that is not hidden needs no faith, only something that is concealed requires faith, and this is because in man’s view the only thing that is revealed is that a great wonder created all of these. These two aspects of the hidden and the revealed are only united in God.

footnotes:
²³ Eelaymim


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/12)


**וַיַּסַּע מֹשֶׁה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.** כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כִּי מִרְיָם הַנְּבִיאָה שָׁרָה אֶת הַשִּׁירָה, אָז הֵבִין כִּי בָּא הָעֵת לִיסַּע מִמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה, כִּי כֵּן הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַש"י בְּעֵת שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, תְּחִילָּה הוּא מַשְׁפִּיעַ לְלֵב הַגְּדוֹלִים וְהַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבָּהֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְפַּשֵּׁט הַדָּבָר עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא לְלִבּוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד הַקָּטָן שֶׁבַּקְּטַנִּים, עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הַזֹּאת אַף בְּלֵב הַנָּשִׁים וְאָז נִשְׁלָם הַחִידּוּשׁ הַזֶּה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּקְבַּע בְּלִבּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָז יִצְטָרְכוּ עוֹד לְהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה חֲדָשִׁים. וְכֵן הָיָה עִנְיַן הַשִּׁירָה בַּתְּחִילָּה הָיְתָה בְּפִי מֹשֶׁה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּפִי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכַאֲשֶׁר נֶאֱמַר "וַתַּעַן לָהֶם מִרְיָם" אָז "וַיַּסַּע מֹשֶׁה" וכו'. הַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּעַתָּה אֵין לָכֶם שׁוּם עֵסֶק בְּזֶה הָעִנְיָן, כִּי כְּבָר גְּמַרְתֶּם מַה שֶּׁצְּרַכְתֶּם, וְעַתָּה אָנוּ צְרִיכִים לְהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.


*“And Moshe had Israel travel from the Red Sea ….”* (Shemot, 15:22)
When Moshe Rabeynu saw that Miriam the Prophetess sang the song at the sea, then he knew that it was time for them to move on from their place. Thus it is with God at a time when He effuses a renewal of the Torah to Israel, first He effuses it to the hearts of the leaders and *tsaddikim* among them. Then afterwards it extends to the hearts of all of Israel, down to the smallest of the small, until this *Kedusha* (holiness) comes to the hearts of the women. Then the renewal is complete, it has been instilled in the hearts of Israel, and then it is necessary for a new renewal of the Torah. Thus it was with the Song at the Sea, first in the mouth of Moshe, and then in the mouths of all Israel, and when it was said, “and Miriam sang for them,” then it followed immediately, “and Moshe had Israel travel.” Meaning that from now on you need not occupy yourselves with this, for you have already finished what was needed, and now we need to renew words of Torah.²⁴ to the hearts of Israel, it proceeds level by level, first by way of the leaders of Israel, just as the Torah was given to Moshe and afterwards he taught it to the leaders of Israel until it finally reached the common folk, just in the same way each soul in Israel first receives in his consciousness [*da’at-Moshe*] until the *Kedusha* is fixed in all his limbs and organs, as it is written [Malachi, 3:16], “then they that feared God spoke with one another, God heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before Him,” meaning that it was carved into the hearts of the children of Israel. We find that the beginning of the effusion of *Kedusha* is in the *Kedusha* of time, and time is only in the possession of God. Therefore women are exempt from positive mitzvot that are bound to time, for female teaches of being fixed in time without activity. However, women are required to perform *mitzvot* that are not bound to time, and this is the sign that this *Kedusha* is fixed in the hearts of Israel.
Knowing this, Moshe had them move on, for whenever it is not yet fixed in the heart of man he can still enter into uncertainty, and enter this *Kedusha* into uncertainty, for it is not yet promised to him, so he may enter it into uncertainty on the possibility that he may gain even more. Yet when it is fixed in his heart, he is not permitted to enter [this *Kedusha* into uncertainty] for now it is certainly his and his possession, so once Moshe saw that the *Kedusha* was fixed in their hearts he had them move on. For truly all the *Kedusha* that man receives, when one receives goodness from God, there is a recognition of His greatness all the time that it resides in his intellect. It is brilliantly clear and cannot be brought to a place that is not God’s will. Yet when it is fixed in the body, then the brilliant clarity is hidden from man and with this added strength he might use it to do an unwarranted activity.
For this reason our sages enacted that we say the *ketoret* (incense offerings) after every [morning] prayer, because the word *ketoret* is related to the word *ketira*, connection, meaning connecting everything, to make sure that this newly gained strength [from the newly gained *Kedusha*] does not enter into a realm that is not God’s will [that it be connected to the will]. And this incident actually caused Miriam to speak against Moshe, so therefore she is called here “Aharon’s sister,” for Aharon was also caught in this [as mentioned in Rashi]. Even though the illumination of God brings strength to man, yet indeed it does not have to be the source of distress of any man, which is a place that is not God’s will. So therefore Moshe had them move onward. (Excerpt from *Giliyon Mei HaShiloach*.)

footnotes:
²⁴ When God effuses Kedusha


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/13)


**וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים בַּמִּדְבָּר וְלֹא מָצְאוּ מָיִם.** הַיְינוּ אַחַר הָעֵסֶק הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בְּיַם סוּף שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה, וְהַהַשָּׂגָה הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהָיְתָה שָׁם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבוֹאָר (מכילתא בשלח פרשה ג') רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה בַּיָּם וְכוּ' וְאַחַר זֶה הָלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים וְלֹא הִשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם הַש"י שׁוּם הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת, וְזֶה "לֹא מָצְאוּ מַיִם", הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא מָצְאוּ שׁוּם תְּשׁוּקָה וְחֵשֶׁק וְנָפַל דַּעְתָּם מְאֹד מִזֶּה, "וַיּוֹרֵהוּ ה' עֵץ" וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן וְאַלְּפֵהּ ה' אָעָא, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה הַש"י מְלַמֵּד אוֹתוֹ עֵצָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁזֹּאת הַשְּׁבִיתָה וְהַנְּיָיחָא בְּלִי שׁוּם עֵסֶק, בָּזֶה נִמְצָא אוֹר וְטוֹבָה מֵהַש"י מֵאַחַר שֶׁזֶּה הוּא רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם זֶה הִיא טוֹבָה עֲמוּקָה. וְזֶה דְּאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תנחומא בשלח כ"ד) עָשָׂה אֶת הַמַּר מָתוֹק, וְאֶל זֹאת הַכַּוָּנָה נִיתַּן לָהֶם שָׁם בְּמָרָה מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת וּפָרָה אֲדֻמָּה וְנִצְטַוּוּ עַל הַדִּינִין. שַׁבָּת מוֹרָה הַיְינוּ רְאוּ כִּי הַש"י נוֹתֵן לָכֶם מִצְוָה שֶׁתַּעַבְדוּ אוֹתוֹ בְּמַה שֶּׁתִּשְׁבְּתוּ וְאִם כֵּן לָמָּה תַּלִּינוּ, וּפָרָה אֲדֻמָּה מוֹרָה עַל הֶעָתִיד, כִּי לֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה ה' אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד וְאָז יִתְבַּטֵּל הָעֲבוֹדָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה אָז שׁוּם כַּעַס. וְדִינִין מוֹרֶה עַל הַסֵּדֶר הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא תַּחְשְׁבוּ עוֹד בְּכָל פַּעַם לִדְחֹק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה לִזְכּוֹת לְכָל זֶה הַטּוֹב, כִּי כָל זֶה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּסֵדֶר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב בְּלִי שׁוּם שִׁינּוּי.


*“… and they went three days into the desert and did not find water.”* (Shemot, 15:22)
After the great event at the Red Sea, and the great understanding received with the revelation of the *Shechina* (Divine Presence) as is explained (Mechilta *B’Shalach*, 3), “a maidservant saw at the splitting of the Red Sea more than the prophets,” they then went for three days with no effusion of the renewal of Torah. This is the meaning of “they did not find water,” that they did not find the longing and the desire for Torah, and were thus despondent. What follows is “and God showed them a branch,” which the Aramaic translation renders “He taught them advice.” The advice was that even this absence of the renewal of Torah (this “dry period”) is also filled with light and goodness from God since it is His will, so it is also goodness of great depth.
On this the Midrash says (Tanchuma, *B’Shalach*, 24), “He made sweet the bitter,” and with this intention he gave them laws of Shabbat, the Red Heifer, and the Justice system at the place named “Mara” (bitter. All three examples will show how the bitter turned to sweet.) “Shabbat” means that they saw how God gave them a way to serve Him even by refraining from action, so there is no reason to complain. “Red Heifer” teaches of the future, for in the future, “He will be one and His name one,” the service will be discontinued and there will be no anger. “The Justice System” teaches of order, for then they will not try to force the hour in order to merit all this goodness, as it must go according to an order so it can be fixed in the heart and immutable.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/14)


**וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע כוּ', וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו תַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֹתָיו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ כוּ'.** אִיתָא בַּזוה"ק (שמות ס':) "אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע" דָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל. "וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו" דָּא צַדִּיק. "וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֹתָיו" דָּא נֵצַח. "וְשָׁמַרְתָּ כָּל חֻקָּיו" דָּא הוֹד וְכוּ'. וּלְקָבְלָא אַרְבְּעָה אִילֵּין נָטוֹרֵי לְהַאי רְשִׁימָא קַדִּישָׁא מֵאַרְבַּע מִלִּין. נָטוֹרֵי דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אִסְתַּמְּרוּתָא דְּנִדָּה. נָטוֹרֵי דְּצַדִּיק אִסְתַּמְּרוּתָא דְּשִׁפְחָה. נָטוֹרֵי דְּנֵצַח אִסְתַּמְּרוּתָא דְּבַת אֵל נֵכָר. נָטוֹרֵי דְּהוֹד אִסְתַּמְּרוּתָא דְּזוֹנָה. אִסְתַּמְּרוּתָא דְּבַת אֵל נֵכָר הַיְינוּ מִמַּה שֶּׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק כְּלָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזוֹנָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁהִיא חֵלֶק מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל רַק שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלְּךָ וְשַׁיָּיךְ לְאַחֵר, וְנִדָּה הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלְּךָ רַק שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנּוֹ, וְשִׁפְחָה הַיְינוּ שְׁטוּת וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵין צֹרֶךְ וְזֶהוּ נָטוֹרֵי דְּצַדִּיק.


*“And He said, if you will surely hearken to the voice of Hashem your God, and do what is Honest in His sight, and diligently adhere to His voice, and guard His laws, then I will not put on you any of the diseases I put upon Egypt, for I am God, who heals you.”* (Shemot, 15:26)
It is written in the Holy Zohar (*Parshat B’Shalach Shemot*, 60b), “If you will surely hearken,’ this is the ‘Knesset Yisrael,’ the community of all Israel [the *Shechina*]. ‘And do what is honest in His eyes,’ this is *tsaddik*, the righteous, [or the *sefirah* of Yesod, foundation or connection]. ‘And diligently adhere to His voice,’ this is, ‘Netsach,’ the *sefira* of eternity or victory. ‘And guard His laws,’ this is, ‘Hod,’ the *sefirah* of majesty or splendor¹.” (A little further the Zohar continues,) “Corresponding to these four there is protection for the holy ‘*roshem*,’ the imprint. Knesset Yisrael is protected by keeping the laws of *nidda*, family purity. The *tsaddik* is protected by keeping away from the ‘*maidservant*’ (adulterous relations). Netzach is protected by keeping away from the daughter of the Gentile. Hod is protected by keeping away from the harlot.” The explanation. “Keeping away from the daughter of the Gentile” means from that which has no portion at all in Israel. “The Harlot” is that which has a portion in Israel but it belongs to another and not to you. “Nidda” means that it belongs to you but its time has not yet come. “The Maidservant” means nonsense and things that are unnecessary, and (refraining from this) guards the *tsaddik*.²⁵

footnotes:
¹ Or empathy. See Kaplan, “Inner Space,” ch. 6-8
²⁵ These could be variously interpreted as pertaining to many different situations, the theme of adultery or licentiousness being only one very important application.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/15)


**וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹל ה' אֱלֹקֶיךָ.** הַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה מוּכָן לִשְׁמוֹעַ בְּקוֹלוֹ זֶה קִיּוּם הַמִּצְוֹת. "וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו תַּעֲשֶׂה" יָשָׁר מוֹרֶה שֶׁתַּעֲשֶׂה פְּקוּדָתוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה וְחִיבָּה, וְתָבִין לְכַוֵּין עוֹמֶק דַּעְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁנִּצְטַוֵּית מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיַּשְׁרוּת לִבְּךָ יוֹרוּךָ כֵּן שֶׁכָּךְ יָשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי הַש"י, כְּגוֹן לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין וּלְהַדֵּר בְּמִצְוָה עַד שְׁלִישׁ בְּמִצְוָה. "וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֹתָיו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ כָּל חֻקָּיו" מוֹרֶה עַל זְרִיזוּת לְקַיֵּים תֵּיכֶף, וְחוֹק מוֹרֶה עַל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי הַשֵּׂכֶל, וְאָז "כִּי אֲנִי ה' רוֹפְאֶךָ" וְתִתְרַפֵּא מִכֹּל.


*“And He said, if you will surely hearken to the voice of Hashem your God.”* (Shemot, 15:26)
That is to say you will be willing to hear His voice, which is the fulfillment of the *mitzvot*. (The author explains each phrase in the verse.) “And that which is honest in His eyes you will do”—“honest” means that you will perform His mitzvot with love and affection, and you will understand how to have in mind the awesome depth of God’s consciousness in order to do more than He commanded you. You have been instructed by the honesty of your heart, for that is honest in the eyes of God. For example, to go beyond what is required for *hiddur mitzvah* (adorning the mitzvah) up to a third more than was commanded. “And diligently adhere to His voice, and keep all His laws” teaches of zeal or alacrity, to fulfill them immediately, and “laws” [*choq*] teaches of that which exceeds the capacity of the intellect, and then “for I am God who heals you,” and you will be healed from all.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/16)


**וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיּוֹתִרוּ אֲנָשִׁים מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים כוּ'.** הָעִנְיָן שֶׁהוּרַם תּוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ מוֹרֶה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם עֲנָוָה פְּסוּלָה וּבְאוּשָׁה, כִּי זֹאת יָדְעוּ כִּי לֹא יַעֲזֹב הַש"י אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַךְ מִדַּאֲגָתָם פֶּן יֵרֵד לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מָן וְלָהֶם לֹא יֵרֵד, וְזֶהוּ עֲנָוָה בְּאוּשָׁה כִּי אֵין הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְהַחֲזִיק עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא גָּרוּעַ מִכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.


*“And they did not listen to Moshe, and some of them left it [the manna] until morning, and it bred worms, and became repulsive.”*(Shemot, 16:20)
That the manna “bred worms and became repulsive” is to say that they had unwarranted and repulsive humility. Even though they knew that God would not abandon them, still they worried that manna would descend to all of Israel but not to them. This is repulsive humility, for no one should see himself as worse than all the rest of Israel.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Beshalach/r/17)


**וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק וַיִּלָּחֶם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְפִידִם.** עִנְיַן חֵטְא רְפִידִים הָיָה שֶׁרָצוּ בְּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת, אַךְ שֶׁאָז לֹא הָיָה בְּאֶפְשָׁרוּת לָבוֹא לְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כֻּלָּם נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה, שְׁרָגָא בְּטִיהֲרָא מַאי אַהֲנֵי. וְזֹאת עִנְיַן מְרִיבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב "עַל נַסֹּתָם אֶת ה' הֲיֵשׁ ה' בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ" וּמִזֶּה הַחֵטְא הָיָה מִלְחֶמֶת עֲמָלֵק, כִּי עֲמָלֵק מַרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיַּחֲטִיאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַמַּטָּרָה אַף כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא יִתְרוֹ, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַמִּדְרָשׁ עַל זֶה (שמות רבה פרשה כ"ז,ג') "לֵץ תַּכֶּה וּפֶתִי יַעְרִים", "וּפֶתִי יַעְרִים" זֶה יִתְרוֹ, שֶׁנָּתַן עֵצָה שֶׁאַף בִּזְמַן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יִהְיֶה נִמְצָא הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת, בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים וְכוּ', וְהַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּהֶם, יִהְיֶה מְנֻשָּׂא עַל הַקָּטָן עַד מֹשֶׁה.


*“And Amalek came and made war with Israel in Rephidim.”* (Shemot, 17:8)
The sin at Rephidim was that they desired a greater status, yet at that time it was not possible to come to any status greater than Moshe, for “of what use is a candle against the bright sky?” [*Hullin*, 60b] This was the quarrel of Israel where it is said “that they tested God saying, is God among us?” The result of this sin was the war with Amalek who senses whenever Israel misses the target even to a hair’s breadth. This is why Yitro came at this time (to fix this), as it say in the Midrash (*Shemot* Rabba, 27:3), “Smite a scorner, and the simple will become prudent. ‘The simple will become prudent,’ is Yitro,”²⁶ who advised to grant others status even in the days of Moshe Rabeynu, when he said “to make princes over thousands,” etc. Then the great among them will be raised over the small, all the way up to Moshe Rabeynu.

footnotes:
²⁶ Rashi says on this verse, “because of the plagues on Pharaoh and the war with Amalek, Yitro became wise and converted.”



#### Yitro

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/1)


**וַיִּשְׁמַע מֹשֶׁה לְקוֹל חֹתְנוֹ וַיַּעַשׂ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָמָר.** הַטַּעַם שֶׁנִּכְתַּב "כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָמָר" בְּסוֹף פָּסוּק, לִהְיוֹת נָקוּד בְּקָמָץ תַּחַת הַמֵּ"ם, גַּם כֵּן לְהוֹרוֹת כִּי גַּם יִתְרוֹ לֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ עוֹמֶק דְּבָרָיו עַד הֵיכָן כִּוֵּן רַק מֹשֶׁה הֵבִין דְּבָרָיו וְזֶה "כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמָר" בְּקָמָץ שֶׁלְּיִתְרוֹ גַּם כֵּן נִתְאַמְּרוּ הַדְּבָרִים, וְלֹא הֵבִין בְּעַצְמוֹ עֵרֶךְ יַקְרוּתָם.


*“And Moshe heard the voice of his father in law [Yitro] and did*col asher amar - *all that he had said.”* (Shemot, 18:24)
At the end of the verse “*amar* - he had said,”²⁷ in Hebrew. is vocalized with the vowel *kamats*, under the *mem* as opposed to the usual *patach*. This is also to signify that Yitro also did not know the great depths of his own words, how far he had intended, only Moshe understood his words. This is, “as he said [*amar*],” vocalized with a *kamatz*, for Yitro also said things to himself, and he himself did not understand how precious they were.²⁸,” “he said,” occurs 595 times in the Scriptures, and in only three instances do we find it vocalized with the vowel *kamatz* under the *mem* instead of a *patach*. See *Bereshit* 18:17, “and God said, shall I hide that which I do from Avraham,” and *Bereshit* 21:1, “and God remembered Sarah as He said.” In the *Torat haNekudot*, where each vowel corresponds to a *sefirah*, the vowel *kamatz* corresponds to the *sefirah* of *keter*, or crown, the highest of the *sefirot*. It has to do with the surrounding light, beyond man’s comprehension. It is described in the liturgical poem “Kel Mistater” [“God, hidden in Himself,” incorporated in the liturgy of the third meal of Shabbat] as the “intellect hidden from all thought.” When connected to this, it signifies something that could be said but not discerned except by the intellect of Moshe Rabeynu. Also requiring further investigation is why the Rebbe chose to say “also to signify,” for surely there are seventy faces to the Torah, even for every vowel, but also in addition to what? Similarly, it says, “Yitro also did not understand,” meaning Yitro, Moshe and whoever else was present when he said this.

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/2)


**וְעַתָּה אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ בְּקֹלִי וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת בְּרִיתִי וִהְיִיתֶם לִי סְגֻלָּה.** עִנְיַן סְגֻלָּה, הַיְינוּ אוֹצָר וּכְלִי קִבּוּל לְקַבֵּל כָּל גִּנְזֵי מְלָכִים, וְכֵן אָמַר הַש"י לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אוֹתָם כְּלִי קִבּוּל כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּנִּיחַ בָּהֶם כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת וְהַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ וְיוּכְלוּ לְקַבְּלָם, וְכֵן אָמַר הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַיְּהוּדִי מִפְּשִׁיסְחָא עַל זֶה הַפָּסוּק, כִּי אַהֲבַת הַש"י לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בְּדֶרֶךְ דְּבַר סְגֻלָּה הַיְינוּ בְּלִי שׁוּם טַעַם.


*“And now, if you will surely hearken to My voice, and you will keep My covenant, then you shall be My most beloved treasure [*segula*]* ….” (Shemot, 19:5)¹. Alternatives are “The designated people,” designated to keep the Covenant, and “the treasured people” whom God treasures as they keep the Covenant. A *Segula* (special treasure) is a vessel of reception for all the hidden wealth of the kings. Thus God said to Israel that He would make them into a vessel of reception in order to place in them all the goodness and blessings that He has, and that they could receive them. The Holy Yehudi of Pshiske²⁹ explains this same verse by saying that God’s love for Israel is in the way of a *segula*, a hidden beloved treasure, as His reasons for this are hidden.³⁰ also refers to a ritual or action that brings God’s goodness, yet with no obvious connection to the good effected, like how smelling the wick of the *havdalla* candle after the *havdalla* ceremony is believed to save one from anger, or a woman biting off the end of the *etrog* (citron) with the stem (*pitom*) after Succot is a *segula* for her to become pregnant. There are countless other *segulot*, another reason why the Jewish People are called, “*Am Segula*.”! The “Tiferret Yosef,” Mordechai Yosef Elazar, great-grandson of the Isbitser, in the first explanation of Shevuot, explains it in this way (first selection on Shevuot, p. 92). “And you shall be My most beloved treasure [*segula*] out of all the peoples,” meaning that then God will show Israel that the love of God for Israel is a kind of *segula*. This is as Rabeynu Moreynu ZL”HH explained in the *Mei HaShiloach*, that *segula* is something without any discernible meaning, like the treasure house of a king, where no man knows how (immensely) precious the treasure really is. In this way God shows Israel that His love for Israel is without any meaning, and His love is above all order of Divine services.

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/3)


**כִּי לִי כָּל הָאָרֶץ.** וְהִנֵּה לְפִי הָעִנְיָן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר כִּי לִי כָּל הָעַמִּים, רַק אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר הַש"י אֶת עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְחֶלְקוֹ מֵאָז אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵסֶק עִם הָאֻמּוֹת וְנָטַל מֵהֶם הַבְּחִירָה וְלֹא יִתָּכֵן לִקְרוֹא לָהֶם שֵׁם מְיֻחָד רַק הֵם נִכְלָלִים בִּכְלַל אֶרֶץ.


*“… for all the earth is Mine.”* (Shemot, 19:5)
According to the context it should have been said, “for all the peoples of the world are Mine.”³¹ However, after God had chosen Israel to be His portion, and basically ended His dealings with the nations of the world, He took from them the power of free choice. Then it was inconceivable to call them by a specific name, and rather included them in the category of the earth.

footnotes:
³¹ This is because the verse just mentioned “peoples”: “you shall be My treasure from all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine.”


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/4)


**וַיְהִי קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר כוּ', מֹשֶׁה יְדַבֵּר וְהָאֱלֹקִים יַעֲנֶנּוּ בְקוֹל.** וְנִלְמַד מִזֶּה בְּמַסֶּכֶת בְּרָכוֹת [מ"ה.] מִכָּאן שֶׁלֹּא יַגְבִּיהַּ הַמְתֻרְגְּמָן אֶת קוֹלוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵהַמְבָרֵךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְהָאֱלֹקִים" כוּ'. וְהוּא תָּמוּהַּ עַיֵּין תּוֹסָפוֹת וְרִי"ף שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ כִּי מִזֶּה נִרְאֶה לְהֵיפֶךְ. וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת מֹשֶׁה הָיָה אוֹמֵר עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אַךְ בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַדָּבָר שֶׁיֵּחָקְקוּ הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּלִבּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶה הָיָה מֵאֵת הַש"י שֶׁהָיָה חוֹקֵק בְּלֵב כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כְּפִי רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן אֲשֶׁר הַש"י כִּבְיָכוֹל נִקְרָא מְתֻרְגְּמָן, הַיְנוּ אַחַר שֶׁיָּצְאוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת מִפִּי מֹשֶׁה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל חָזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְחָקַק אוֹתָם בְּלִבָּם, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַגְבִּיהַּ הַמְתֻרְגְּמָן אֶת קוֹלוֹ כוּ', כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה בִּיכֹלֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַחֲקוֹק הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, יוֹתֵר מִכֹּחַ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, אַךְ כְּתִיב "וְלֹא קָם עוֹד נָבִיא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמֹשֶׁה", וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא הֵאִיר הַש"י לְשׁוּם נֶפֶשׁ יוֹתֵר מִלְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם. וְזֶהוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַגְבִּיהַּ הַמְתֻרְגְּמָן אֶת קוֹלוֹ יוֹתֵר כוּ' הַיְינוּ יוֹתֵר מִמַּדְרֵגוֹת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.


*“… and the voice of exceedingly loud shofar … Moshe spoke, and God answered him in a voice.”* (Shemot, 19:16–19)
It is explained in the Talmud, *Berachot* (45a), “from here we derive that the translator will not raise his voice louder than the one reading the verse from the Torah.”³² “God answered him in a voice,” was like the translator reading after him at the same volume. This would seem quite unusual, and the sages of the Tosafot and R. Itschak Alfasi (the “Rif”) proposed that the verse would imply the opposite.³³ While Moshe indeed spoke the Ten Mitzvot to Israel, the root of the matter was that with the giving of the Torah at Sinai, the mitzvah of Torah study was fixed into the hearts of Israel. This was done by God, who imprinted into the heart of each and every one according to His blessed will. In this way God is called, as it were, the translator, meaning that after the Ten Mitzvot went forth from the mouth of Moshe to Israel, the Holy One, blessed be He, went back and imprinted them into the hearts of Israel. This is “the translator will not raise his voice more than the reader,” for truly it was in the power of the Holy One, blessed be He, to carve the words of Torah into their hearts according to His blessed power, much more than Moshe Rabeynu could. However, it is written, “never again would there be a prophet in Israel as great as Moshe,” so God could not shine His light into any soul of Israel more than he did with Moshe Rabeynu. This is, “the translator will not raise his voice more than the reader,” meaning more than the level of Moshe Rabeynu.³⁴

footnotes:
³² In the days of the Mishna, and still today in many Yemenite congregations, at the public Torah reading, each verse is followed with the translation of Onkles into Aramaic, which was then the spoken language of the day.
³³ If God Himself is answering Moshe, then obviously the voice of the Creator and power of all the worlds should take precedence.
³⁴ For God, “the translator,” would never raise His voice, meaning illuminate His power into, anyone more than He did for Moshe, “the reader.”


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/5)


**אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹקֶיךָ.** וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר אֲנִי, כִּי אִילּוּ הָיָה כְּתִיב אֲנִי, הָיָה מַשְׁמַע שֶׁגִּילָּה אָז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת כָּל אוֹרוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת וְלֹא יוּכְלוּ אַחַר כָּךְ לְהַעֲמִיק בִּדְבָרָיו, כִּי כְּבָר גִּילָּה הַכֹּל, אַךְ הַכַּ"ף מוֹרֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת וְרַק דְּמוּת וְדִמְיוֹן הוּא לְהָאוֹר שֶׁיְּגַלֶּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֶעָתִיד, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיַּשִּׂיג הָאָדָם יוֹתֵר עַמְקוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה יִרְאֶה שֶׁעַד עַכְשָׁיו הָיָה בַּחוֹשֶׁךְ. וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז הַיּוֹם וְהַלַּיְלָה, הַיּוֹם הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹתֵחַ שַׁעֲרֵי הַחָכְמָה לָאָדָם וְהַלַּיְלָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְדַמֶּה הָאָדָם שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַכֹּל בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁהִשִּׂיג הוּא כְּלַיְלָה נֶגֶד הַיּוֹם הַבָּא אַחֲרָיו וְכֵן לְעוֹלָם, וּמִמֵּילָא הַכֹּל הוּא לַיְלָה נֶגֶד הָאוֹר שֶׁיִּפְתַּח הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֶעָתִיד. וְזֶה שֶׁנִּסְמַךְ מַאֲמַר "לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה לְךָ פֶסֶל" וְאִיתָא בַּזוה"ק (שמות פ"ז:) מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב "פְּסָל לְךָ" עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר "לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה לְךָ פֶסֶל" וְלֹא תַעֲבֵיד לָךְ אוֹרַיְיתָא אוֹחֲרָא. וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי מִלַּת פֶּסֶל הוּא דָּבָר מְחוּתָּךְ בְּמִדָּה וְקֶצֶב וּבְהַשְׁלָמָה בְּלִי חֶסְרוֹן שׁוּם דָּבָר בָּעוֹלָם וְזֹאת אֵינוֹ נִמְצָא רַק בְּתוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, אֲבָל בְּשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי אֵין בָּאֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן דָּבָר כָּזֶה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַגָּמוּר, כְּמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָ' [רות רבה פרשה ג',ב'] שֶׁאָמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא גַּם אֲנִי יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת תּוֹרָה כְּמֹשֶׁה וְגָזַר שֶׁלֹּא יְבַעֲרוּ אֵשׁ ג' יָמִים וּבְתוֹךְ כֵּן רָאָה עָשָׁן יוֹצֵא מִבַּיִת אֶחָד וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ הַקֵּיסָר כִּי שַׂר אֶחָד חָלָה וְהוּכְרַח לְהַתִּיר לוֹ. וְהָאֻמְנָם כִּי גַּם אֶצְלֵינוּ הַדִּין עַל פִּי תּוֹרָתֵנוּ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה כִּי פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת, אַךְ הַחִילּוּק כִּי הַמְחַלֵּל שַׁבָּת עַל פִּי פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ אֵינוֹ מִתְנַגֵּד לַתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, כִּי גַּם זֹאת נִצְטַוֵּינוּ שֶׁפִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ יִדְחֶה שַׁבָּת. וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה'" נִרְמַז הַצִּיווּי שֶׁל "הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ" וְלָכֵן הַתּוֹרָה כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל הַרְפַּתְקָאוֹת שֶׁיַּעַבְרוּ, וְאוֹרָהּ מַקִּיף כָּל הָאוֹפַנִּים וְכָל הַהִתְהַוּוּת שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְהַוּוֹת, וְזֶה אֵין בְּכֹחַ שׁוּם אָדָם לַעֲשׂוֹת, וְזֶה שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ בַּזוה"ק עַל "לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה לְךָ פֶסֶל" הַיְינוּ בְּמִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה, "וְכָל תְּמוּנָה" הוּא בְּמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, כִּי לֹא נִגְלָה לָאָדָם שׁוּם דָּבָר עַד תַּכְלִיתוֹ.


*“Anochi Hashem E-loheicha—I am Hashem your God ….”* (Shemot, 20:2)
The word *Ani* is not used for “I” (but rather, *Anochi*). Had it been written “*Ani*,” the meaning would have been that the Holy One, blessed be He, had revealed His light to Israel in all its completeness, and then they could not have reached deeply into His words, for He would have already revealed everything. However the additional letter *Caf* in “*Anochi*,” teaches that it is not in a state of completeness, yet rather a conception of how the light that the Holy One, blessed be He, would be revealed in the future.³⁵ added before a word means “like.” The more a man apprehends in the depths of the Torah, the more he will then understand that until now he was in darkness. This is hinted at in the night and the day. “Day” means that God opens the gates of wisdom for man, and “night” means that man should never imagine that has completely apprehended Godliness, for all he has attained is like night in comparison to the day that follows. So it goes on forever, and it follows that all is night in the face of the light that the Holy One, blessed be He, will open in the future.
This is why the verse that follows immediately is, “do not make any graven [carved] image,” on which it is said in the Holy Zohar (*Shemot*, 87b), “since it was first written, ‘carve for yourself [two tablets],’ therefore it says, ‘do not make any carved image,’ meaning do not make another Torah.” The word *pesel*, “carved image,” means something with a definite form and measurement, in a state of completeness with nothing lacking. This is found only in the Torah of Moshe Rabeynu. However it is impossible for the mortal intellect to fashion anything in complete perfection.
On this it is written (Ruth Rabba, 3:2), “Caesar said to Rabi Yehoshua ben Hanina, ‘I too can make a Torah like Moshe,’ and he decreed that no fire be kindled for three days. (As if to say, “God decrees that you do not light fire for one day? I can decree it for three days.”) During this time he saw smoke rising from a house, and they explained to Caesar that a certain government minister was sick and it was necessary to permit him fire.” For indeed, according to our Holy Torah the law is that saving a life supersedes the laws of Shabbat, yet the difference (with us and the example of Caesar) is that one who violates Shabbat to save a life is not going against the Holy Torah, for thus was it also commanded that saving a life takes precedence over the laws of Shabbat. So, too, in all places where it is, “a time to do for God,” (*Tehilim*, 119:126), fulfilling Gods word, it is also hinted, as the verse continues, “they have made Your law null and void.”³⁶ Therefore the Torah includes all the possible combinations of events that may occur, everything and its opposite, and its light surrounds all the possibilities and all the experiences that may evolve. No man has the power to do this. This is the explanation of the Holy Zohar on “do not make any carved form,” meaning positive mitzvot, and “any image,” the prohibitive mitzvot, for nothing is revealed to man until it reaches its completion.

footnotes:
³⁵ Caf
³⁶ A situation that would require the suspension of that law, such as how we suspend the laws of Shabbat in order to save a life.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/6)


**אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹקֶיךָ.** בַּזוה"ק אִיתָא וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים הוּא בְּרָזָא דְּחָמֵשׁ חָמֵשׁ, וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן הָעִנְיָן בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת, "אָנֹכִי" הוּא מְקוֹר הַחַיִּים, "ה'" הַיְינוּ גְּבוּרָה וְהוּא הַמְהַוֶּה כֹל, "אֱלֹקֶיךָ" הַיְינוּ מִדַּת אֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר הַש"י מַנְהִיג בָּהּ אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ, "אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם" הַיְינוּ שֶׁתֵּדַע אַף בְּעֵת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְךָ אֵיזֶה צַעַר חָלִילָה לֹא תִקְצֹף נֶגֶד הַש"י, "מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים" הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִּהְיֶה מְשׁוּקָּע בְּהַטּוֹבָה, וְגַם אַחַר זֶה נֶאֱמַר שֶׁאַל תְּדַמֶּה כִּי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלּוּ שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי לְךָ בְּנָקֵל הֵם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם, לֹא כֵן כִּי צָרִיךְ לָזֶה בֵּירוּרִים גְּדוֹלִים, וְזֶה נֶגֶד זֶה נֶאֱמַר, "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" הוּא נֶגֶד "אָנֹכִי" שֶׁלֹּא תַחְשׁוֹב כִּי נִמְצָא גָּוֶון חַיִּים חָלִילָה חוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ. "אֲחֵרִים" הוּא נֶגֶד "ה'", הַיְינוּ גָּוֶון גְּבוּרָה. "עַל פָּנַי", הוּא נֶגֶד "אֱלֹקֶיךָ" דְּהַיְינוּ גָּוֶון אֱמֶת וְהוּא רַק לְפָנִים לֹא מִן הָאֱמֶת הָאֲמִיתִּי. "לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה לְךָ פֶסֶל וְכָל תְּמוּנָה", הוּא נֶגֶד "אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם". "מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים", הוּא נֶגֶד "אֲשֶׁר בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל" וְכוּ', כִּי שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ וְיַמִּים הֵם עִיקַּר בִּנְיַן הָעוֹלָם, וְגַם נִמְצָא בָּעוֹלָם תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד, כִּי קִנְאָה הוּא נִכְלָל בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם כִּי לְאֵלּוּ הוּא מְקַנֵּא, וְהֵם גַּם כֵּן חָמֵשׁ כְּנֶגֶד הֶחָמֵשׁ הָאֲמוּרִים לְמַעְלָה. "לֹא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לָהֶם", הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִּהְיֶה כָּפוּף תַּחְתָּם. "וְלֹא תָעָבְדֵם", הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִּרְצֶה לִהְיוֹת מוֹשֵׁל עֲלֵיהֶם. וְיֵשׁ ג' מַדְרֵגוֹת, עוֹלָם שָׁנָה נֶפֶשׁ, וּכְנֶגֶד כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ רָזָא דְּחָמֵשׁ, כְּנֶגֶד עוֹלָם וְהוּא מָקוֹם, הוּא מַה שֶּׁדִּבַּרְנוּ עַד כָּאן. וּכְנֶגֶד שָׁנָה הַיְינוּ זְמַן הוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּרָזָא דְּחָמֵשׁ חָמֵשׁ הַיְינוּ פֶּסַח הוּא נֶגֶד "אָנֹכִי", שָׁבוּעוֹת הוּא נֶגֶד "ה'", סֻכּוֹת הוּא נֶגֶד "אֱלֹקֶיךָ", רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הֵם נֶגֶד "אֵל קַנָּא" שֵׁם אֵל מוֹרֶה עַל חָכְמָה, קַנָּא פֵּירוּשׁ כַּעַס הַיְינוּ שֶׁכַּעֲסוֹ הוּא בְּחָכְמָה. נֶפֶשׁ הַיְינוּ אָדָם יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן רָזָא דְּחָמֵשׁ וְהֵם, אָבוֹת וּבָנִים שִׁלֵּשִׁים רִבֵּעִים וְלַאֲלָפִים. הֲרֵי הַכֹּל בְּרָזָא דְּחָמֵשׁ חָמֵשׁ וְהָבֵן כִּי עָמוֹק הוּא.


*“I am Adonai your God ….”* (Shemot, 20:2)
It is written in the Holy Zohar, “and the tree of life is in the secret of five, five.” “*Anochi*, I am,” is the source of life. “*Adonai*” is *Gevurah*—strength, which brings all into being. “*E-loheicha*, Your God” is the measure of truth in which God runs His world. “Who brought you out of the land of Egypt” means that even at a time of anguish, may God protect us, still refrain from becoming angry at God. “From the house of bondage” means do not become immersed in niceties, and after this the Torah warns not to imagine that what I ask from you is easy, rather you need to struggle to become pure. Each of these five corresponds to one of the next five. “You shall not have” corresponds to “Anochi,” so as not to think that there is even a hue (or appearance) of life aside from Him.³⁷ “Other gods,” meaning a hue of *Gevurah*—strength.³⁸ “Before Me” corresponds to “your God,” meaning a hue of truth that is only superficial, and not part of truth at its deepest level.³⁹ “Do not make any sculpted idol or image” corresponds to “who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”⁴⁰ “From the house of bondage” corresponds to “which is in the heavens above,” etc.
The heavens, the earth, and the seas are the principal forms in the construction of the world, and the world also contains desire and honor. Jealousy is also included in these two, as it is for these that He is jealous, and they are also the five corresponding to five mentioned above. “Do not bow down to them” means do not be subdued by desire and honor. “Do not serve them” means do not desire to rule over them. Existence is divided into three levels—place, time, and soul. Everything discussed thus far has been in the category of place. Corresponding to time, with the festivals during the course of the year, there is also the secret of “five, five.” Pesach is “Anochi—I.”⁴¹ Shevuot is “Hashem.”⁴² (strength), and at Mount Sinai it is said that, “Moshe heard from the mouth of Gevurah.” Succot corresponds to “Elo-heicha, your God.”⁴³ is likened to the clouds of glory that followed us in the desert, an awesome sight to witness that inspires the fear of God, and so too the name “E-lohim” teaches of God’s attribute of judgment that is the root of this fear. Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur correspond to “E-l Kana, a jealous God,” for the name “E-l” teaches of *Chochma* (wisdom)¹ and “jealous,” meaning anger, that is to say that His anger is in (the *sefirah* of) *Chochma*. In the category of soul, meaning person, there is also the secret of five, namely, “the fathers, the children, the third, the fourth [generations], and the thousandth [generation]” (*Shemot*, 20:5). Thus, all in the secret of “five, five.” Deep contemplation is required to understand this.

footnotes:
³⁷ Re: “New Age,” or more properly, ancient; idolatry of earth forces.
³⁸ Meaning also taking a subordinate force in the world as the prime force.
³⁹ “Before me,” is literally “at my face,” and the word for “superficial” is literally “to the face.”
⁴⁰ The land of idolatry.
⁴¹ In the first redemption God first made himself known to us as a nation.

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/7)


**אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹקֶיךָ.** הִנֵּה בִּמְצִיאוּת הָאָדָם נִמְצָא ה' כֹּחוֹת וְהֵם, הִרְהוּר, מַחְשָׁבָה, רָצוֹן, מַעֲשֶׂה, דִּבּוּר. אִם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בָּא לָאָדָם כַּסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּה בָּא בְּהִרְהוּר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָרְדָה לְמַחְשָׁבָה וּלְרָצוֹן, אָז יְהֵא בָּטוּחַ שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַזּוֹ הוּא מֵרְצוֹן הַש"י וְנִצְמַח מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים, אַךְ אִם בָּא לָאָדָם הַסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה, שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּה בָּא רָצוֹן לַלֵּב וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָרְדָה לְמַחְשָׁבָה אָז צָרִיךְ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַזּוֹ בֵּרוּרִין, כִּי אוּלַי גּוּף צְמִיחַת הָרָצוֹן נוֹלַד בּוֹ מֵאֵיזֶה נְגִיעָה מֵחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה. וְהִנֵּה נֶגֶד אֵלּוּ ה' כֹּחוֹת נִתְּנוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת לְבָרֵר אֵלּוּ הַה', כִּי גַּם עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת נֶחְלְקוּ לְחָמֵשׁ נֶגֶד חָמֵשׁ לְכָל דַּרְגָּא חָמֵשׁ, נֶגֶד מִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה. "אָנֹכִי" הוּא נֶגֶד הִרְהוּר כִּי בְּעוֹד הַדָּבָר בְּהִרְהוּר, אֵין לוֹ יְדִיעָה כְּלָל רַק כְּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חֵשֶׁק לַעֲשׂוֹת מַה וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ עֲדַיִן מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה, וְאַף לִקְטַנִּים שֶׁאֵינָם בְּנֵי דֵעָה יֵשׁ לָהֶם הִרְהוּר וּבְעֵת שֶׁהָאָדָם יָשֵׁן גַּם כֵּן יֵשׁ הִרְהוּר רַק בְּלִי הַכָּרָה וּתְפִיסָה בְּשֵׂכֶל וְנֶגֶד זֶה הָיָה הַדִּבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" נֶגֶד מִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה, כִּי "אָנֹכִי" כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁרְצוֹן ה' שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹכָם, כִּי בְּמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהֵם סוּר מֵרָע יֵשׁ לָאָדָם תְּפִיסָה בַּשֵּׂכֶל, אֲבָל מִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין שַׁיָּכוּת לָאָדָם שׁוּם תְּפִיסָה וְשֵׂכֶל בּוֹ. אַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" הַיְנוּ שֶׁלֹּא תַחְשֹׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ הֲוָיָה אַחֶרֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם חוּץ מִמֶּנִּי, וְזֶה נֶגֶד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה. "לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת שֵׁם" וכו' הַיְנוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִּדְחֶה לְשׁוּם דָּבָר בָּעוֹלָם לְחָשְׁבוֹ לְחִנָּם, כִּי יֵשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיצוֹץ קְדֻשָּׁה רַק יֵשׁ בּוֹ פְּנִימִיּוּת וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת וְתֵדַע לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב מִן הָרַע, וְהַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד הַמַּחְשָׁבָה וְהֵם שְׁנֵי פְּסוּקִים אֶחָד נֶגֶד מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁל הַמַּחְשָׁבָה וְהַשֵּׁנִי נֶגֶד לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁל הַמַּחְשָׁבָה. "זָכוֹר" וְ"כַבֵּד" נֶגֶד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, "לֹא תִרְצָח" וְ"לֹא תִנְאָף" נֶגֶד הָרָצוֹן, וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב הַמַּעֲשֶׂה קֹדֶם לָרָצוֹן, כִּי בְּאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יֶחֱטָא הָאָדָם בְּמַעֲשֶׂה יַקְדִּים לַחְקֹר וְלִתְלוֹת בַּמַּחְשָׁבָה וְהַיְנוּ בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים שֶׁלּוֹ וְצָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה לְרַפֵּא אֶת שָׁרְשׁוֹ וְלֹא יִתְלֶה הַחֶסְרוֹן בְּהָרָצוֹן, כִּי הָרָצוֹן יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת שֶׁאֲחֵרִים הִכְנִיסוּ לוֹ. "לֹא תִגְנֹב" וְ"לֹא תַעֲנֶה" הֵם נֶגֶד הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁהִצְטָרְכוּת הַדִּבּוּר הוּא רַק לְהִתְחַבְּרוּת לְזוּלָתוֹ שֶׁלְּעַצְמוֹ אֵין צֹרֶךְ בְּהַדִּבּוּר כְּלָל, וְהַתּוֹרָה הִיא בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת, וּלְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה הָעוֹלָם, פֵּרוּשׁ "לֹא תִגְנֹב" הַיְנוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִמְנַע דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה מִן תַּלְמִידוֹ (סנהדרין צ"א:) וְזֶה שַׁיָּךְ אַף בַּמַּלְאָכִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וּמְקַבְּלִין דֵּין מִן דֵּין", כִּי בַּמַּלְאָכִים יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגוֹת וּמִי שֶׁהוּא בְּמַדְרֵגָה גְּבוֹהָה יֵשׁ לוֹ תַּקּוּפוּת יוֹתֵר מִמִּי שֶׁהוּא קָטָן מִמֶּנּוּ. וְלָזֶה הַקָּטָן יֵשׁ לוֹ יִרְאָה יוֹתֵר עַל כֵּן מְקַבְּלִין דֵּין מִן דֵּין, וְ"לֹא תַעֲנֶה" הוּא לְהֵפֶךְ מִ"לֹּא תִגְנֹב" שֶׁלֹּא לְהַרְבּוֹת דְּבָרִים עַל כֵּן אֵלּוּ הַב' הֵם נֶגֶד הָעֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּדִּבּוּר. "לֹא תַחְמֹד" הוּא הַלֹּא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבְּהִרְהוּר וְשַׁיָּךְ אֵצֶל "אָנֹכִי", אַךְ שֶׁאִם הָיָה הָאָדָם נִשְׁלָם בְּבֵרוּר הַהִרְהוּר בִּשְׁלֵמוּת לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְהִתְבָּרֵר בִּשְׁאָר הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת, עַל כֵּן לֹא יוּכַל לִכְתֹּב אֵצֶל "אָנֹכִי" הַלֹּא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁל הִרְהוּר רַק אַחַר שֶׁמִּתְבָּרֵר בְּמַחְשָׁבָה וְרָצוֹן וּמַעֲשֶׂה וְדִבּוּר אָז יֵצֵא הַהִרְהוּר מְבֹרָר וּלְכָךְ נִכְתַּב בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה.


*“I am Hashem your God ….”* (Shemot, 20:2)
There are five faculties in human existence; gleam (“musing” or “inkling”), thought, will, action, and speech. If a man’s action is a result of these five stages, beginning in the gleam⁴⁴, which is more vague than a thought. It is here understood as a gleam that sprouts from the subconscious, as opposed to a tangible thought. and descending afterwards to thought and will, then he may be sure that this action is God’s will, having sprouted from the source of life. However, if the action came about by a different order, where first the will came to the heart and descended to thought, then this action needs *birurum* (refinements) as the gleam from the will that conceived it may have been tainted by worldly desires. God gave us the Ten Mitzvot in order to refine these five faculties.
The Ten Mitzvot are also divided into five against five, the five positive mitzvot on the right tablet in opposition to the five prohibitions on the left. “*Anochi*—I am the Lord” corresponds to the gleam, where the knowledge is still murky and he still doesn’t know what to do. This is like someone who has the vague desire to do something. Small children have such gleams that they cannot articulate. Similarly when a person sleeps he has such gleams of thought that cannot be grasped by the intellect.
All of this corresponds to the first of the positive mitzvot, “*Anochi*,” for the Divine utterance “*Anochi*” includes within it all the positive mitzvot of the Torah and God’s will dwells within them. The five prohibitions were all given in order “to turn from evil” so therefore man must be able to grasp them in his intellect, yet as the five positive mitzvot are the very locality of God, it is not conceivable that he may have any real understanding of them. After that it is said, “you shall not have any other gods,” meaning that you are not to think that there is another Source of Being⁴⁵ has the same letters as “being”—*HAVAYE* in Hebrew. in the world besides Me, and this corresponds to the faculty of thought. “Do not take God’s name in vain” means not to push aside anything in the world as unnecessary and useless.
Everything that God created has a spark of *Kedusha* (holiness) within it, only it has an internal and an external nature, and you need to know how to separate the good from the bad. This verse also corresponds to thought, for there are two verses, one corresponding to a positive commandment of thought, and another corresponding to a prohibition of thought. “Remember the Shabbat” and “Honor your father” correspond to the faculty of action. “Do not kill” and “do not commit adultery” correspond to will. The reason the mitzvot signifying action precede the mitzvot signifying will is that if one sins in action, God forbid, he will go back and ponder it and find some thought to hold responsible for it, meaning in the very source of his life. So then he must “do *teshuva*” [return to the way of God] in this regard, sincerely mending his ways and thus healing his roots. He is not to find fault in the will, for others could have entered this will into his mind.¹ “Do not steal” and “do not bear false witness” correspond to speech. This is because the entire need for speech is only in order to communicate with others, as by himself he has no need for speech. 
The Torah exists in all of the worlds, so above this world “do not steal” means not to prevent the Torah from reaching one’s students (*Sanhedrin*, 91b). This applies even to angels, as it is said of them, “and they receive permission from one from the other.”⁴⁶ There are also different levels among the angels. An angel on a higher level will have greater strength that one on a lower level. Yet the one on the lower level has greater reverence for the power of the one on the higher level, therefore “they receive one from the other.” 
“Do not bear false witness” is the opposite of “do not steal.” Bearing false witness is to speak too much and therefore these two correspond to the positive and negative mitzvot of the faculty of speech. “Do not covet” corresponds a prohibition in the gleam of thought, and belongs with “*Anochi*.” Yet if one could achieve a perfect *birur* (clarification) in this gleam, he would have no need of *birur* in the other faculties. Therefore the prohibition in the faculty of gleaming could not be written together with “*Anochi*,” but rather only after thought, will, action, and speech have been refined, then the gleaming would emerge refined. This is why coveting appears at the end of the Ten Mitzvot.

⁴⁴ The word used is hirhur
⁴⁵ The name of God YHVH
¹ This is puzzling for what does it matter if it was his original will to sin or if he was led astray. Yet you might say the fault is theirs and not his. His will was high jacked.
⁴⁶ This is the rendering of the Aramaic translation of Yesahya 6:3, “and they called one to another.”


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Yitro/r/8)


בְּפָסוּק "אָנֹכִי" נִמְצְאוּ כָּל הָאוֹתִיּוֹת חוּץ מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת ג"ז ח"ט ס"פ"ק. ג"ז מוֹרֶה עַל הַהַתְחָלָה שֶׁהָאָדָם מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ גֵּר שֶׁבָּא לְהִתְגַּיֵּר צָרִיךְ לְמַעֵט כָּל הֲנָאוֹתָיו וּלְהִזָּהֵר אַף בְּדִקְדּוּק מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים וְזֶהוּ גֵּז לְשׁוֹן גְּזִיזָה. וְאַחַר כָּךְ ח"ט הַיְנוּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה עַל קִיּוּם הַמִּצְוֹת מִבְּלִי לַחֲטֹא. וְאַחַר כָּךְ ספ"ק הַיְנוּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שֶׁיִּמָּצֵא בּוֹ יִרְאָה בְּנִסְתָּרוֹת לִבּוֹ.


The verse “Anochi—I am Hashem your God” contains all the letters of the Hebrew alphabet except *Gimel”Zayin* (“GeZ”), *Chet”Tet* (“CheT”), and *Samech”Peh”Koof* (“SaPheK”). “GeZ” (to shear) teaches of the beginning when one first accepts upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, such as the convert who, when he comes to observance, must first limit (“shear”) his enjoyment of worldly pleasures and take great care of the details enumerated by the codifiers of the Law.⁴⁷. Afterwards comes *CheT*, which means sin, as he must take care to guard himself and keep the *mitzvot* without sinning. Following this is *SaPheK*, meaning uncertainty and fearing what might be hidden in his heart.⁴⁸

footnotes:
⁴⁷ Like a sheep, he is shorn from all his coarseness and refined into a vessel for Torah and Kedusha
⁴⁸ This implies stages of a process. First there is renouncing the vanities and pleasures of the world, and adhering to the details of the Divine law. Second, one must guard himself in his adherence from possible sin. And third, he must take care that even though he sees himself as a vessel for the Torah from the outside, he may well harbor hidden deficiencies that may prevent him from his refinement.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 9
