⁷⁶ And how is incense the connection of all things? Besides the similarity in the letters of ketoret


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Tetzaveh 6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Tetzaveh/r/6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Tetzaveh/r/6)


כָּל הַכֵּלִים הָיוּ שֶׁל עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים מְצֻפִּים זָהָב חוּץ מֵהַכַּפֹּרֶת וּמְנוֹרָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם זָהָב טָהוֹר בְּלֹא תּוֹךְ שֶׁל עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים. כִּי יָדוּעַ שֶׁהַמִּשְׁכָּן וְכֵלָיו רוֹמְזִים לְקוֹמַת צוּרַת הָאָדָם, וּבְכָל הָאֵבָרִים רְשׁוּת לָאָדָם לְכַוֵּן לְטוֹבַת עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן בִּפְעֻלָּתוֹ כְּמַאֲמַר חֲזַ"ל (פסחים ס"ח:) "מֵעִיקָּרָא כִּי עָבֵיד אִינִישׁ לְגַרְמֵיהּ הוּא דְּעָבֵיד", וְלֶעָתִיד יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָשָׂה לְגַרְמֵיהּ הָיָה רַק כְּמוֹ הַתְחָלָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ לָבֹא עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִשְׁמָהּ וּלְהוֹצִיא אוֹר מִתּוֹךְ חֹשֶׁךְ כַּנֶּאֱמַר (יואל ד',י"ח) "וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת נַחַל הַשִּׁטִּים" וְכוּ׳, אֲבָל הַכַּפֹּרֶת שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד הַלֵּב, וְהַמְּנוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא נֶגֶד עֵינַיִם, בָּזֶה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם שְׁמִירָה מְאֹד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נְקִיִּים וּמְבֹרָרִים בְּלִי שׁוּם צַד נְגִיעָה מִצִּדּוֹ לְשׁוּם טוֹבַת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כִּי אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא [ירושלמי ברכות פרק א', ה"ה] הָעַיִן וְהַלֵּב הֵם תְּרֵי סַרְסוּרֵי עֲבֵרָה, עַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד. וְהִנֵּה בֶּאֱמֶת צָרִיךְ הָעַיִן לִהְיוֹת מֻפְשָׁט מִכָּל תַּאֲוַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְרַק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּלִי לְהַנֶּפֶשׁ כְּמוֹ זְכוּכִית בַּר וְנָקִי שֶׁהַנֶּפֶשׁ תַּבִּיט דֶּרֶךְ הָעַיִן עַל כָּל דָּבָר וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ תְּבָרֵר אוֹתוֹ אִם הוּא טוֹב תְּקַבְּלוֹ וְאִם לָאו לֹא תְקַבְּלוֹ, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהָעַיִן עַצְמוֹ שׁוּם תַּאֲוָה לְחֶמְדַּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אָז אֵין הָעַיִן כְּלִי לְהַנֶּפֶשׁ רַק הִיא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְחוֹמֵד לְכָל עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא יוּכַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב מֵהָרַע, וְלָכֵן צִוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְבֹרָרִים, הָעַיִן יִהְיֶה נָקִי וּמֻפְשָׁט מֵחֶמְדּוֹת מִמֵּילָא גַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ לֹא יַחְמֹד רַק לְדָבָר שֶׁהוּא בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.


All of the vessels of the Mishkan were made of acacia wood inlayed with gold, except for the *caporet* (the covering for the Holy Ark) and the menorah, where says specifically that they should be made of pure gold, and not filled with acacia wood. It is known that the Mishkan and its vessels hint at the upright form of man, and for each limb man has the right to see to his own well-being, as it says in the Gemara (*Pesachim*, 68b), “in the first place, when a man does something, he is doing it for himself.”⁷⁷ In the future, God will make it clear that the action that he did for himself was only in the sense of “if a person does a mitzvah but not for the sake of Heaven, eventually he will do it for the sake of Heaven.” Eventually he will bring the light out of the darkness, as it is said (Yoel, 4:18), “and a fountain shall come forth from the house of God, and shall water the valley of Shittim [which means acacia wood].”⁷⁸
Yet the caporet, which corresponds to the heart, and the menorah, which corresponds to the eyes, with these a man must be especially vigilant that they are clean and refined, not corrupted in any way from his own desire for the pleasures of this world. This is as it is said in the Jerusalem Talmud (*Berachot*, 1:5), “the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin. The eye sees and the heart lusts.” But indeed the eye must be stripped of all the lusts of this world, and used as a pure vessel for the soul, like a clear glass through which the soul looks at the world and decides whether it is good and to receive it, or whether it is evil and to reject it. Yet, when within the eye itself there is any desire or lust for the pleasures of this world, then the eye is not a vessel for the soul, but rather a free agent, free to lust after the affairs of this world. Then the soul does not have the opportunity to distinguish the good from the evil. Therefore God commanded to be completely refined. The eye shall be clean and stripped of vain lusts, and then it will follow that the soul will only desire that which is God’s will.

footnotes:
⁷⁷ The Gemara is talking about the mitzvah of the study of Torah, that foremost he is studying for his own benefit, and only after this for the good of the rest of the world.
⁷⁸ This means that all the vessels made from acacia wood are like actions that may be for selfish motives to gratify different parts of the body now, but will be refined for the sake of Heaven in the future.



#### Ki Tisa

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/1)


**וְרָחֲצוּ יְדֵיהֶם וְרַגְלֵיהֶם.** עִנְיַן רְחִיצַת הַכֹּהֲנִים מֵהַכִּיּוֹר הוּא עִנְיַן סִילּוּק וַהֲסָרַת נְגִיעָה, כִּי רְחִיצָה מוֹרָה עַל זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אֵצֶל עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה (דברים כ"א,ו') "וְרָחֲצוּ זִקְנֵי כוּ' וְאָמְרוּ יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכוּ" כוּ', וְהוּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם נְגִיעָה וְחֵלֶק בְּזֶה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וְגַם הַכֹּהֵן הָעוֹבֵד הוּצְרַךְ לִרְחִיצָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּסִיר נְגִיעָתוֹ וּמְבַטֵּל דַּעְתּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵד רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ. וְכֵן אֲשֶׁר נִצְטַוֵּינוּ לִטּוֹל יָדֵינוּ שַׁחֲרִית וְקוֹדֶם סְעוּדָה, הוּא גַּם כֵּן קוֹדֶם שֶׁיַּתְחִיל הָאָדָם לַעֲסוֹק בְּצָרְכֵי הַגּוּף צָרִיךְ תְּפִלָּה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, בְּאִם שֶׁיָּבֹא לְיָדוֹ דָּבָר מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אָז הוּא מְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּטּוֹל וְיָסִיר אֶת תַּאֲוָתוֹ מִזֶּה, וְאַף גַּם בִּדְבַר הֶיתֵּר נִמְצָא גַּם כֵּן טוֹב וְהִיפּוּכוֹ, כִּי בְּאִם יֹאכַל הָאָדָם דְּבַר הֶיתֵּר וְיֵלֵךְ אַחַר כָּךְ בְּכֹחַ הַזֶּה וְיַעֲשֶׂה עֲבֵירָה, אָז נִגְלָה הַדָּבָר כִּי לֹא קִבֵּל כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּזֶה הַדָּבָר, וְעַל זֶה הוּא הָרְחִיצָה שֶׁהוּא תְּפִלָּה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבְּכָל דָּבָר לֹא יְקַבֵּל רַק כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב שֶׁנִּמְצָא, כִּי נַחֲלָה הַבָּאָה לוֹ לָאָדָם מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר מַתְנֶה עָלֶיהָ שֶׁלֹּא יִירָשֶׁנָּה, וְלָזֶה קָבְעוּ לוֹמַר פָּרָשַׁת הַכִּיּוֹר קוֹדֶם הַתְּפִלָּה וְקוֹדֶם פָּרָשַׁת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפַּלֵּל רַק עַל מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ.


*“And from it Aharon and his sons shall wash their hands and feet.”* (Shemot, 30:19)
When the *Cohanim* washed from the laver (*kiyor*) in the Holy Temple they did so in order to remove and kind of *negia* (personal motive, partiality) Washing teaches of this, as we find in the passage of the beheaded heifer (Footnote *Devarim*, 21:6, the *eiglah arufah*, where the elders first take general responsibility for the death and then wash their hands, declaiming to God “our hands did not spill this blood), “and the elders of the city shall wash their hands over the heifer that is beheaded.” Here they are saying that they are clean from *negia* associated with the death and have no portion in it. So too, the Cohen who serves needs to wash, meaning that he removes any *negia*in his life, nullifying his own mind and will before God’s will. This means that all his service is only what God desires.
So it is with how we are commanded to wash in the morning and before a meal, for before one begins to fulfill the needs of the body he needs to pray. If some worldly matter comes upon him and leads him astray, God forbid, he then prays to God to remove any desire he might have not only from a sin, but even from something permitted that might be a mixture of good and its opposite. For if one were to eat in a way that is permitted to him and then go on and use the energy from this to transgress, then it is made clear that he did not receive any goodness from the food. 
Concerning this we have ritual washing, which is a kind of prayer that we only see goodness from our actions. We pray to God that our behavior is on condition, the condition being that only good comes out of it. It is for this reason that in the morning service our sages included this passage about washing from the laver before we say the daily sacrifices, meaning that we ask that even what we pray for is only what God desires.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/2)


**וַיִּפֶן וַיֵּרֶד מֹשֶׁה מִן הָהָר וּשְׁנֵי לֻחֹת הָעֵדֻת בְּיָדוֹ לֻחֹת כְּתֻבִים מִשְּׁנֵי עֶבְרֵיהֶם כוּ'.** בַּגְּמָרָא (שבת ק"ד.) אִיתָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִסְדָּא לֻחוֹת כְּתוּבִים מִשְּׁנֵי עֶבְרֵיהֶם שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים מִבִּפְנִים וּמִבַּחוּץ כְּגוֹן נְבוּב בּוּבָן רַהַב בָּהָר סָרוּ וְרָס, וְהוּא שֶׁרַבִּי חִסְדָּא אָמַר כִּי יֵשׁ כֹּחַ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה לְשַׁנּוֹת אֶת לֵב הָאָדָם מֵהִיפּוּךְ לְהִיפּוּךְ, נְבוּב הַיְינוּ אָדָם שֶׁהוּא נָבוּב וְרֵיק מִדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה נַעֲשֶׂה עַל יָדָם מָלֵא בִּינָה וְהוּא נְבוּב בּוּבָן. רַהַב הַיְינוּ אָדָם שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא תַּאֲוֹת וְחֶמְדּוֹת זָרוֹת כַּמְבוֹאָר בַּגְּמָ' (זוהר שמות ק"ע:) שַׂר שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם רַהַב שְׁמוֹ וּמִצְרַיִם הָיוּ שְׁטוּפִים בְּזִמָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עמוס ח',ח') "וְנִגְרְשָׁה וְנִשְׁקְעָה כִּיאוֹר מִצְרָיִם" שֶׁמֵּימָיו הָיוּ עֲכוּרִים, וְזֶה מוֹרֶה עַל מַחְשְׁבוֹת תַּאֲוֹת רָעוֹת, וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה יוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת וְלִהְיוֹת מוּרָם וּמוּבְדָּל מִכָּל חֶמְדָּה, כִּי בָּהָר מוֹרֶה עַל זֶה, כִּי בָּהָר לֹא נִמְצָא לַחְלוּחִית כְּמוֹ בָּעֵמֶק, וְכֵן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יַעַן כִּי הָיָה מוּבְדָּל מִכָּל חֶמְדָּה לְכָךְ אָמַר (בראשית כ"ב,י"ד) "הַיּוֹם בְּהַר ה' יֵרָאֶה". סָרוּ הַיְינוּ אָדָם שֶׁהוּא בְּכַעַס כִּי סַר הוּא לְשׁוֹן כַּעַס כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מלכים א' כ"א,ד') "סַר וְזָעֵף" וְכֵן בַּגְּמָרָא (בבא מציעא נ"ט:) מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסּוֹרוֹ רַע הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כַּעַס וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה יוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לִבּוֹ לְטוֹב וְלִהְיוֹת מוּבְדָּל מִשּׁוּם כַּעַס, כִּי מוֹרָס הוּא מִלְּשׁוֹן רַךְ כַּמְבוֹאָר בַּגְּמָרָא מְמָרֵס בַּדָּם, כִּי מוֹרָס נוֹפֵל עַל דָּבָר רַךְ וְכֵן (יחזקאל מ"ו,י"ד) "לָרֹס אֶת הַסֹּלֶת".


*“And Moshe turned and descended from the mountain, and two tablets of the testimony in his hand, written from both sides.”* (Shemot, 32:15)
It is written in the Gemara (*Shabbat*, 104a), “R. Chasda says, they were written from both sides for they were read from within and without. That is, ‘*navuv* [empty], *boban*,’ ‘*rahav* [arrogance or rage], *behar* [on the mountain],’ ‘*saru, veras*.’” (Footnote: Both Rashi and Tosafot ask why these words used as they don’t appear in the ten mitzvot? The Mei HaShiloah offers an answer.) R. Chasda is saying that the Torah has the power to change the heart of man from one side to the opposite. *Navuv* means one who is hollow, or empty of Torah, and so by means of them he is filled with understanding, and this is, “*navuv, boban*” (*boban* is connected to *Binah*, or understanding). *Rahav* means someone who is filled with desires and external lusts, as it is written (Zohar, *Shemot*, 170b), “the angel of Egypt was called *rahav*, and Egypt was steeped in perversity,” as it says (Amos, 8:8), “banished and immersed like the Nile of Egypt,” whose waters were brackish, which teaches of evil thoughts of desire. By means of the Torah he can be separated from all lusts, which is the inner meaning of *behar* (on the mountain), for you do not find moisture on the mountain that is deep in the valley.
So too with Avraham Avinu, since he was separated from all lust, thus it was said (at the binding of Yitschak, *Bereshit*, 22:14), “for it is said to this day, on the mount Hashem was seen.” *Saru*, meaning anger, for *sar* is an expression of anger, as it is written Kings 1, 21:4), “and Achav came home ‘*sar ve’zaef*,’ sullen and angry,” and on this it says in the Gemara (*Bava Metsia*, 59b), “why does the Torah warn against distressing the convert in forty-eight places? For it may turn him [*saro*] to evil,” meaning he has anger, and by means of the Torah he may change his heart to the good, and separate himself from any anger, for *moras*, (*veras*, the opposite of *saru*) meaning rubbed or stirred, as the Gemara says, “did they ever stir the blood of the sacrifice before you?” for this occurs in a tender place (the opposite of anger), as it is said (Yechezkel, 46:14), “to stir [*laros*] the fine flour.”


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/3)


**וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל ה' רְאֵה אַתָּה אֹמֵר אֵלַי כוּ', וְאַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ יְדַעְתִּיךָ בְשֵׁם וְגַם מָצָאתָ חֵן בְּעֵינָי כוּ' וַיֹּאמֶר גַּם אֶת הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ אֶעֱשֶׂה כִּי מָצָאתָ חֵן בְּעֵינַי וָאֵדָעֲךָ בְּשֵׁם.** לִהְיוֹת מֹשֶׁה בְּבַקָּשָׁתוֹ אָמַר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָדַע אוֹתוֹ בְּשֵׁם, הַיְינוּ שֶׁבָּרָא אוֹתוֹ בְּמִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת לְקַבֵּל חֵן מֵאֵת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְחֵן הוּא מַתְּנוֹת חִנָּם שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא אוֹתוֹ בְּמִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת וַעֲבוּר זֶה מָצָא חֵן, וּתְחִילָּה "יְדַעְתִּיךָ בְשֵׁם" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּחַר בּוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁבָּחַר בַּאֲבוֹתֵינוּ אַף טֶרֶם מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁעָשׂוּ, הוּטְבַּע בָּהֶם מִדּוֹת אֲשֶׁר גַּם בָּנוּ נִשְׁאֲרוּ, כִּי הַשָּׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת אֲשֶׁר אֲנַחְנוּ מְעוּטָּרִים בָּהֶם רַחְמָנִים וּבַיְישָׁנִים גּוֹמְלֵי חֲסָדִים, אֵינָם מִצַּד מַעֲשֵׂינוּ הַטּוֹבִים רַק מִצַּד אֲבוֹתֵינוּ הַקְּדוֹשִׁים שֶׁהוֹרִישׁוּ לָנוּ קְדוּשָּׁתָם, וְכֵן אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי תְּחִילָּה יָדַע אוֹתוֹ בְּשֵׁם וְאַחַר כָּךְ מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ הֵשִׁיב לוֹ לְהִיפּוּךְ, כִּי בִּתְחִילָּה מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָדַע אוֹתוֹ בְּשֵׁם, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִכִּיר מִדּוֹתָיו אֲשֶׁר בְּאִם הָיָה כְּלִי לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה, אָז יַחְפּוֹץ וְיִשְׁתּוֹקֵק בְּכָל עֵת לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה חֲדָשִׁים וְזֶהוּ מְצִיאוּת חֵן הַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּחְפּוֹץ וְיִשְׁתַּדֵּל תָּמִיד לְמַתְּנוֹת חִנָּם וְעַל זֶה בָּרָא אוֹתוֹ בְּמִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דניאל ב', כ"א) "יָהֵיב חָכְמְתָא לְחַכִּימִין" כְּמַאֲמַר הַגְּמָרָא (יומא י"ב.) עַל בִּנְיָמִין וְהָיָה בִּנְיָמִין הַצַּדִּיק מִצְטַעֵר עָלֶיהָ לְבוֹלְעָהּ לְפִיכָךְ נַעֲשָׂה אוּשְׁפֵּיזַכְנָא לַשְּׁכִינָה, הַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִכִּיר בּוֹ כִּי בְּאִם יִבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּחֶלְקוֹ יַחְפּוֹץ מְאוֹד לְקַבֵּל גַּם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לְחֶלְקוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה אוּשְׁפֵּיזַכְנָא.


*“And Moshe said to God, see, you say to me, bring this people up … And God said to Moshe, I will also do as you have spoken, for you have found favor in My sight, and I will know you by name.”* (Shemot, 33:12–17)
God addressed Moshe’s request by saying that God knows Moshe by name, which means that He created Moshe with good attributes in order to receive the *Chein*, the Grace of God. *Chein* itself is a free gift, that God created him with good attributes and owing to this he is in God’s favor (a play on words; to be in favor is also *chein*). First (for in verse 12 Moshe makes first mention of), “You said, I knew you by name,” that He chose him as he chose all the Patriarchs, even before they performed good deeds. And these attributes that were imprinted in their souls yet remain in us, for the three attributes that crown us (as a people), compassion, modesty, and giving loving-kindness, are not contingent on our good deeds but comes rather from the holiness of our Patriarchs, which they inherited to us.
This is why Moshe first said that God knew him by name, and then after, he found favor with Him, whereas when God in His answer to Moshe formulates it in the opposite way, first saying that he has found favor in His eyes, and after saying that He knew him by name. This means that God recognized his attributes, which are a vessel for receiving the Torah. In this way he would at all times desire and long for new words of Torah, and this is how he finds favor with God, meaning that he will always desire and strive for the “free gifts” (the reception of *Chein*). Towards this He created him with good attributes, as it is written (Daniel, 2:21), “give wisdom to the wise.”
This concerns what we find in the Gemara of Binyamin (*Yoma*, 12a), “Binyamin the *Tsaddik* was greatly concerned that the Holy of Holies fall in his domain. [For the Temple mount falls both in the portions of Yehuda and Binyamin, yet the Holy of Holies was in the portion of Binyamin, and because of his holy “distress” to take care of the area, the Altar was also allotted in his portion.] For this he was made a host for the Divine presence.” That is to say, since God recognized that if the Holy Temple (the house of the Holy of Holies) would be built in his portion then he would greatly desire that the outside Altar also be in his portion (the “free gift”). For this (desire) he was made its host.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/4)


**וַיֹּאמַר פָּנַי יֵלֵכוּ וַהֲנִחֹתִי לָךְ.** הוּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵשִׁיב לוֹ בְּעֵת שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ מֵאִתּוֹ הַלְּבוּשׁ הַנִּרְאֶה כְּפָנִים שֶׁל זַעַם יִהְיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנַיְיחָא. כִּי יֵשׁ לְבוּשִׁים לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמַּרְאֶה מִדּוֹת קִנְאָתוֹ וּבְעֵת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בַּמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת אָז גַּם הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא עַמּוּד הַדּוֹר הוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת כְּגוֹן פִּנְחָס בְּדוֹרוֹ וְאֵלִיָּהוּ בְּדוֹרוֹ, כִּי הַצַּדִּיק הוּא לְבוּשׁ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאָז נִרְאִים כִּמְקַטְרְגִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּגוֹן אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמַר (מלכים א' י"ט,י') "כִּי עָזְבוּ בְרִיתְךָ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל", אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָסִיר מֵאִתּוֹ זֶה הַלְּבוּשׁ וְיִתְנַהֵג בְּמִדּוֹת טוּבוֹ וְרַחֲמָיו, גַּם לְהַצַּדִּיקִים יֵרָאֶה כִּי בְּעוֹמֶק מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ לֹא מָצָא בְּשׁוּם זְמַן ח"ו שׁוּם כַּעַס וְאָז גַּם לֵב הַצַּדִּיקִים יִהְיֶה שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.


*“And He said, My presence shall go with you, and I shall give you rest.”* (Shemot, 33:14)
God answered Moshe that at a time that a “garment” goes forth from Him that seems like a face of anger, then Israel shall be at peace. God has garments to He shows His jealousy, and at the time when God is in this attribute then the *Tsaddik*, who is the pillar of his generation, also takes on this attribute, like Pinchas in his generation or Eliyahu in his generation. This is because the *Tsaddik* is the garment of God, and then it seems as if he is bringing accusations against Israel, as when Eliyahu said (Melachim 1, 19:10), “for the children of Israel have abandoned Your covenant.” Then when God removes this garment, and conducts the world through His goodness and compassion, then the *Tsaddik* shows that at the depth of his consciousness he was never angry, God forbid, and then the heart of the *Tsaddikim* will also be at peace with Israel.

**וַהֲסִירוֹתִי אֶת כַּפִּי וְרָאִיתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָי וּפָנַי לֹא יֵרָאוּ.** בַּגְּמָרָא (ברכות ז'.) מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶרְאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין, תְּפִלִּין מְרַמְּזִין עַל דְּבֵיקוּת וְחִיבּוּר כְּמוֹ (בראשית ל',ח') "נַפְתּוּלֵי אֱלֹקִים". הַיְינוּ שֶׁאָנוּ מְקוּשָּׁרִין בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אַף כִּי יַעֲבוֹר עָלֵינוּ מָה לֹא נִתְפָּרֵד מִמֶּנּוּ, וּתְפִלִּין דְּמָארֵי עָלְמָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ "מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל" (ברכות ו'.) הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִשְׁתַּבֵּחַ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מִתְקַשְּׁרִין בּוֹ וְגַם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְשָׁר בָּהֶם אַף כִּי יֶחֱטְאוּ לֹא יִהְיֶה נִתּוּק מֵהֶם אַהֲבָתוֹ. "וּפָנַי לֹא יֵרָאוּ" הַיְינוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה לְמֹשֶׁה אֶת כָּל הַנַּעֲשֶׂה מִן הֶעָבָר רָאָה בָּרוּר כָּל מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה בּוֹנֶה מִזֶּה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְזֶה "וְרָאִיתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָי" הַיְינוּ הֶעָבָר, "וּפָנַי לֹא יֵרָאוּ" הַיְינוּ הַהוֹוֶה לֹא הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, מִפְּנֵי כִּי כָּל קַבָּלוֹת הָעוֹנָשִׁין עַל יָדוֹ נֶאֶמְרוּ, וְלָכֵן לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל כִּבְיָכוֹל לְהַרְאוֹת לוֹ הַהוֹוֶה אֵיךְ שְׁלֵימוּתוֹ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַהוֹוֶה, וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר (בגמ') (מדרש תנחומא חקת ח') "דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֶמְרוּ לְמֹשֶׁה נֶאֶמְרוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא" שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "כָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁרָאָה כָּל הַתְּפִלִּין שֶׁגַּם בְּהַהוֹוֶה נִרְאֶה לוֹ כִּי לֵב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׁלֵם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזֶה שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּגְּמָרָא (מכות ז'.) אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא "אִלּוּ הָיִיתִי בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין לֹא הָיָה נֶהֱרָג אָדָם מֵעוֹלָם", לְפִי שֶׁרָאָה כִּי תָּמִיד לֵב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׁלֵם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל.


*“And I shall remove My hand, and you shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen.”* (Shemot, 33:23)
It is said in the Gemara (*Berachot*, 7a), “this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moshe the knot at the back of his head *tefillin*.”⁷⁹ tied at the base of the skull.*Tefillin* hints at intense closeness and connection, as it is said (*Bereshit*, 30:8), “the wrestlings of God.”⁸⁰—“wrestlings” has the same Hebrew letters as *tefillin*. This means that we are connected to the Holy One, blessed be He, and no matter what happens to us, we will not separate from Him. In the *tefillin* of the Master of the Universe it is written, “Who is a nation so great as to have God so close to it?” This means the God praises himself in that Israel is so connected to Him, and also that God is connected to them, even if they sin He will not disengage his love for them. “But My face shall not be seen” means that God showed Moshe all the events that happened in the past and saw clearly what God had built out of each action. This is “You shall see My back.”⁸¹ “But my face shall not be seen” means that the Holy One, blessed be He, did not show Moshe what was happening in the present, because all the acceptances of punishment were transmitted through him.⁸² Therefore He could not, as it were, show him the present, meaning how God was completely reconciled with Israel in the present.
This is as it is said (Midrash Tanchuma, *Chukat*, 8), “that which was not said [revealed] to Moshe Rabeynu was said to Rabbi Akiva, as it is said [Iyov, 28:10], ‘his eye saw all the preciousness.’” This means that He showed Rabbi Akiva the whole *Tefillin*, and showed him how God was reconciled with Israel also in the present. This is as it is mentioned in the Gemara (*Makkot*, 7a), “Rabbi Akiva said, If I had been a member of a Sanhedrin, no one would ever have been sentenced to death.” This is because he saw how the Holy One, blessed be He, was always reconciled with Israel.

footnotes:
⁷⁹ The knot of the head tefillin
⁸⁰ Naftulei
⁸¹ “Back” represents the past; “face” the present.
⁸² And would thus confront irreconcilable differences.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/6)


**וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אִם אֵין פָּנֶיךָ הֹלְכִים אַל תַּעֲלֵנוּ מִזֶּה.** כִּי מֹשֶׁה בִּקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר אַף בְּעוֹד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּלְּבוּשׁ הַזֶּה (האמור למעלה בד"ה ויאמר וכו') גַּם אָז אִם יֶחֱטָא שׁוּם אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יַגִּיעַ הַחֵטְא לְעוֹמֶק הַלֵּב וְלֹא יָבוֹא הִתְרַשְּׁלוּת בְּדַעְתּוֹ פֶּן הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נָסוֹג מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּקְרָא "זֶה אֵלִי", וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר "וְנִפְלִינוּ אֲנִי וְעַמְּךָ מִכָּל הָעָם אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה". כִּי הַהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאוּמּוֹת לֹא יִהְיֶה תָּלוּי רַק בְּמִצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, כִּי גַּם הֵם יוּכְלוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מַעֲשִׂים שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם גָּוֶון טוֹב, אַךְ אַף בְּעֵת שֶׁאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֶחֱטָא גַּם הַחֵטְא לֹא יִהְיֶה כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָאוּמּוֹת וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ רַק מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְעוֹמֶק לִבּוֹ יִהְיֶה נִקְשָׁר וְנִדְבָּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְזֶה בֵּיאֵר בַּגְּמָרָא (ברכות ל"ב:) "וַתֹּאמֶר צִיּוֹן עֲזָבַנִי ה' וַה' שְׁכֵחָנִי" אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הוֹאִיל וְאֵין שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִּסֵּא כְּבוֹדֶךָ שֶׁמָּא לֹא תִּשְׁכַּח לִי מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֵגֶל, אָמַר לָהּ "גַּם אֵלֶּה תִשְׁכַּחְנָה", אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמָּא תִּשְׁכַּח לִי מַעֲמַד הַר סִינַי, אָמַר לָהּ "וְאָנֹכִי לֹא אֶשְׁכָּחֵךְ". וּבֶאֱמֶת לָמָּה בָּזֶה הֵשִׁיב שֶׁיִּשְׁכַּח וּבָזֶה לְהֵיפֶךְ, אַךְ כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֵגֶל הָיָה כִּי רָצוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַרְאֶה לָהֶם אֶת הַסֵּדֶר הַמְסוּדָּר אֶצְלוֹ לְכָל מִדּוֹתָיו לְדוֹרוֹת, בְּאֵיזֶה זְמַן יְנַהֵג אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ בְּמִדָּה זוֹ וּבְאֵיזֶה זְמַן בְּמִדָּה אַחֶרֶת, וְלֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ בְּכָל יוֹם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לָהֶם בְּאֵיזֶה דָּבָר וּבְאֵיזֶה מִדָּה יִבְחַר עַתָּה, רַק יְגַלֶּה לָהֶם הַכֹּל בְּפַעַם אַחַד וְיֵלְכוּ בִּדְרָכָיו לָבֶטַח תָּמִיד, וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה נוֹגֵעַ הַחֵטְא רַק מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ לְפִיכָךְ נִשְׁכַּח. אַךְ הַמִּצְוֹת הֵמָּה מֵעוֹמֶק הַלֵּב, לְזֵכֶר עוֹלָם יִהְיֶה, וְלַאֲשֶׁר נִסְמַךְ פָּרָשַׁת שַׁבָּת לְפָרָשַׁת הָעֵגֶל, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת שׁוֹרֶשׁ חֵטְא הָעֵגֶל בָּא לָהֶם בְּעֵת שֶׁעָסַק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בְּפָרָשַׁת שַׁבָּת, כִּי שַׁבָּת מְרַמֵּז עַל יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת וְאָז לֹא יוּצְטָרְכוּ לִתְפִלָּה כִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יַרְאֶה לְעֵין כֹּל אֶת סֵדֶר מִדּוֹתָיו כִּי בִּלְתִּי רְצוֹנוֹ לֹא נַעֲשֶׂה שׁוּם דָּבָר בָּעוֹלָם, וְהֵם הִרְגִּישׁוּ כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹסֵק לְהַנְחִיל לָהֶם הַטּוֹב הַזֶּה, וְהָיָה חֶטְאָם לְפוֹעַל שֶׁעָשׂוּ אֶת הָעֵגֶל, כִּי עֵגֶל הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁלַם עֲדַיִין וְצָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּין עוֹד עַד שֶׁיּוּשְׁלַם, וְגַם רָצוּ בָּזֶה קוֹדֶם הַזְּמַן כִּי הַטּוֹב הַזֶּה יַנְחִיל ה' לָנוּ אַךְ לֶעָתִיד.


*“And he said to Him, if Your presence does not go with me, then do not raise us up from this.”* (Shemot, 33:15)
Moshe asked God that even while He is still dressed in this garment (see the previous discussion of “and He said, My presence shall go with you”) that even then, if any one of Israel sins, that the sin would not reach the depth of the heart. That even then, the sinner’s mind would not become so weak that he would, God forbid, remove himself from God, of whom he said (*Shemot*, 15:2), “this is my God,” and of whom he said, “and You have separated both Me and Your people from all the peoples on the face of the earth.” The difference between Israel and the nations is not only based on the performance of *mitzvot* and good deeds, for they too can perform actions that seem to be good. Yet the difference is, even when one of Israel sins, then the sin will not be like that of the nations.⁸³ Rather it will only have effect from the edge and outside, with the depth of the heart remaining connected, even united, with God.
This is as it is written in the Gemara (*Berachot*, 32b) in the verse (Yeshayahu, 49:14), “And Zion said, has Hashem forsaken me? Has Hashem forgotten me? Can a woman forget her suckling child, the child of her womb? These too will be forgotten, but I will not forget you.” “The community of Israel said before God, Master of the Universe! Since there is no forgetfulness before Your Throne of Glory, perhaps you will not forget the sin of the golden calf? God answered, ‘these too will be forgotten.’ The Community of Israel said, ‘perhaps you will forget the day we stood at Mount Sinai?’ God answered, “but I [who said “I—Anochi” at Mount Sinai] will not forget you.’”
It may be asked of this, why does God say that he will forget one incident and remember the other? Truly, the sin of the golden calf happened because God wanted to show them the order that He had arranged in His Divine plan for all His attributes for all generations. He showed them that at one time He would conduct the world through one attribute, and at another time through a different one. This way they would not have to pray at each moment for God to show them which mode and which attribute He was now choosing, but rather He gave them all of His attributes at once (*Shemot*, 34:6–7), and they could proceed on their way ever confident, and since the sin would only reach from the edge and outward it was therefore forgotten. The *mitzvot*, however, are from the depth of the heart, an eternal memorial. There is a special reason why the passage discussing Shabbat is juxtaposed to the sin of the golden calf. This is because the root of the sin of the golden calf came to them at the very moment that the Holy One, blessed be He, and Moshe Rabeynu were involved in the study of Shabbat.
Shabbat hints at the day that is entirely Shabbat (the redemption), and at that time prayer will not be necessary because the Holy One, blessed be He, will make it clear to all the order of His attributes,⁸⁴ for without His will nothing at all could be done in the world. Down below they felt vibrations that God was preparing to bestow unto them this complete good, and the effect in their actions was the sin of the golden calf. This is because a calf is something that is not yet complete,⁸⁵ and one must wait for it to reach its completion. In the same way they wanted to receive the “day that is entirely Shabbat” before its time, for God will only bestow unto us this complete good in the future.

footnotes:
⁸³ With the nations the sin reaches the depth of their soul.
⁸⁴ And at that time all will know God’s will with clarity.
⁸⁵ It is not yet a cow.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/7)


**וַיֹּאמֶר אֲנִי אַעֲבִיר כָּל טוּבִי עַל פָּנֶיךָ.** לֶהֱיוֹת כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בִּקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לוֹ הָעוֹמֶק הַנִּמְצָא בַּהַנְהָגָה, מִפְּנֵי מָה יֵשׁ לְכָל אָדָם מַעֲלָה וּמַדְרֵגָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְאֶחָד לֹא יִשְׁוֶה לַחֲבֵירוֹ, לָזֶה הֵשִׁיב לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא "אֲנִי אַעֲבִיר כָּל טוּבִי" כוּ', הַיְינוּ שֶׁאַרְאֶה לְךָ כִּי אֵין אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ אֶת מַעֲלָתוֹ וְהַטּוֹב הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ וְתִרְאֶה בְּמַה שֶּׁהוּא בּוֹחֵר לוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְקָרָאתִי בְשֵׁם ה'" הַיְינוּ שֶׁאַרְאֲךָ עוֹמֶק מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַה שֶּׁהֲכִינוֹתִי וְחִלַּקְתִּי לְכָל אֶחָד בִּשְׁעַת הַתְחָלַת הַבְּרִיאָה, כִּי שֵׁם הוי"ה מוֹרֶה עַל הַתְחָלַת הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהוּא מְהַוֶּה הַכֹּל וְאַתָּה תִּרְאֶה כִּי כָל אֶחָד לֹא בָּחַר לוֹ רַק חֶלְקוֹ אֲשֶׁר הֲכִינוֹתִי לוֹ. וְזֶהוּ "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר" כוּ' הַיְינוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁחֲנַנְתִּיו וְרִיחַמְתִּיו מִקּוֹדֶם בָּזֶה אוֹשִׁיעַ אוֹתוֹ לְטוֹב לוֹ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה לֹא יַגִּיעַ לְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ כְּמַאֲמַר הַמִּדְרָשׁ (קהלת רבה פרשה ג',ט') "כָּל אוּמָּן לָא מַשְׁרִין לֵיהּ אֶלָּא אֵצֶל בַּעֲלֵי אוּמָּנֻתוֹ".


*“And He said, I will cause all of My good to pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of Hashem, and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and, and I will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”* (Shemot, 33:19)
Since Moshe asked God to show him the depth of how He conducts the world, then why does each man have his own rank and level, where no one is equal to another?⁸⁶ To this the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, “I will cause all of My good to pass before you,” which means that no man knows his rank and the good that is his portion, and he shall see this through what he chooses for himself.⁸⁷ After this it says, “and I shall proclaim the name of Hashem,” meaning that I will show the depth of My consciousness in what I have apportioned for each one from the beginning of creation.
This is because “the name of Hashem” teaches of the beginning of creation when He brings all into being.⁸⁸, has the same root as the word *mehave*, “bring into being.” Then you shall see that what each one chooses for himself is exactly the portion that God has prepared for him. This is “I will be gracious with whom I will be gracious,” meaning with that which I have been gracious and merciful with him from the beginning is exactly that which I will use to save him for his own good. By means of this one will not arrive at the portion of his fellow, as in the saying of the Midrash on the verse (Kohellet, 3:9), “what does one profit in working in that which he labors?”—“Each artisan is only permitted to dwell with his fellow craftsmen” (Kohellet Rabba, 3:9).

###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/8)


**וַיְמַהֵר מֹשֶׁה וַיִּקֹּד אַרְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּחוּ וכו׳.** בַּגְּמָרָא (סנהדרין קי"א.) מָה רָאָה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם רָאָה. וְהִנֵּה בֶּאֱמֶת מַה יִּתְרוֹן לְאֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם בְּאִם הֶעָוֹן אֵינוֹ נִמְחָק הֲלֹא כָּל הַחַיִּים שֶׁיִּחְיֶה אֵינוֹ רַק חַיֵּי שָׁעָה וְכָל הַמִּצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה לֹא יַגִּיעוּ גַּם כֵּן לָעֹמֶק, כִּי לֹא יֵעָשֶׂה מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים, וְגַם בָּנִים אֲשֶׁר יוֹלִידוּ לֹא יִחְיוּ גַּם כֵּן רַק עַד שֶׁיְּמֵי הַחַיִּים יַגִּיעוּ, כִּי אֵין בְּשׁוֹרְשָׁם רַק חַיֵּי שָׁעָה. אַךְ יַעַן כִּי הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כִּי בָּעֹמֶק אֵין שׁוּם כַּעַס לְפָנָיו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַכַּעַס אֵינוֹ רַק מֵהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, אַךְ כִּי הַכַּעַס הַזֶּה הָיָה יָכוֹל לְכַלּוֹת אוֹתָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֶרְאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה שֶׁיַּאֲרִיךְ אַפּוֹ גַּם כֵּן וְאָז יִשָּׁאֵר בְּקִרְבָּם חַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים וְכָל הַמִּצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ יִהְיוּ לָעַד, וְגַם בָּנִים אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלְדוּ לָהֶם לָעַד יִהְיוּ, כִּי הַמִּצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְגַם הַהוֹלָדָה הִיא מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים וִיהִי קַיָּם לָעַד, וְעַל זֶה בִּקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם "יֵלֶךְ נָא ה׳ בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ" כִּי שֵׁם א"ד"נ"י מְחַיֵּב עֲבוֹדָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁנָּשִׁיב בְּלִבֵּנוּ לַעֲבֹד אוֹתוֹ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ קַיָּמִים וְזֶה "וְסָלַחְתָּ לַעֲוֹנֵנוּ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁתּוֹצִיא מֵאִתָּנוּ הַחֵטְא מְעַט מְעַט וְיִשָּׁאֵר בְּלִבֵּנוּ רַק הַטּוֹב, "וּנְחַלְתָּנוּ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּקַּח אוֹתָנוּ לְנַחֲלָה וְאָז בְּכָל מִדּוֹתֵינוּ נוּכַל לַעֲבֹד אֶת ה׳.


*“And Moshe made haste, and bowed his head to the ground, and worshipped. And he said, if I have found favor in Your eyes I pray that Adonai shall go in our midst, for they are a stiff-necked people. Forgive our iniquities and sins and take us as Your inheritance.”* (Shemot, 34:8)
It is written in the Gemara (*Sanhedrin*, 111a), “What did Moshe see [that, immediately after receiving the thirteen attributes of mercy he ran and bowed in worship]? He saw the Long Suffering [patient].” Truly, what is the use of God’s attribute of patience if the sin is not erased? Is not the entire length of his life only temporary, and even all the *mitzvot* and good deeds that he does will not reach the depths, for they have not been done from the source of life? And even the children he fathers will only live out the number of their days, for their source is only in fleeting existence? However, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him that in the depths He bears no anger towards Israel, and it is only from the edge and outward, for such anger could eradicate them, God forbid.
Then the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moshe that He would also be long-suffering with them, that eternal life would remain within them, and all the *mitzvot* and good deeds that they did would last forever, and the children that they would have would continue forever. For their *mitzvot*, good deeds, and progeny were all rooted in the source of life, and would endure forever. Upon seeing this, Moshe then asked, “I pray that Adonai will go in our midst,” for the name “Adonai” necessitates service, meaning, let such service dwell in our hearts that we may perform *mitzvot* and good deeds that endure forever. This is “pardon our iniquity,” meaning to slowly remove the sin from our heart that only the good will remain. “And take us for Your inheritance,” meaning, take us as an inheritance and then we will be able to serve God with all of our qualities.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/9)


**אֱלֹהֵי מַסֵּכָה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ.** מַסֵּכָה הַיְינוּ כְּלָלִים וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַכָּתוּב בְּעֵת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְךָ בִּינַת הַלֵּב מְפֹרֶשֶׁת אָז לֹא תַבִּיט עַל הַכְּלָלִים לְהִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּיהֶם רַק בְּבִינַת לִבְּךָ תֵּדַע בְּכָל פְּרָט דָּבָר אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ בְּהַר הַכַּרְמֶל, וְעַיֵּין בְּפָרָשַׁת חֻקַּת עַל פָּסוּק "וַיִּסְעוּ מֵאֹבוֹת וַיַּחֲנוּ" כוּ׳, וְשָׁם נִתְפָּרֵשׁ דָּבָר זֶה בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב.


*“Do not make molten gods.”* (Shemot, 34:17)
“Molten or graven images” means principles. The verse is saying that at a time when your heart receives an explicit understanding, then do not look to the principles and act according to them; rather, you shall know down to the detail how to act according to the understanding of your heart. We find an example of this with Eliyahu at Mount Carmel. See below in *Parshat Chukot* on the section beginning, “and they camped at Ovot,” and there the matter is well explained.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/10)


**אֶת חַג הַמַּצּוֹת תִּשְׁמֹר כוּ׳ לְמוֹעֵד חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב.** אָבִיב הוּא לְשׁוֹן אָב שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַתּוֹלָדוֹת הַיְינוּ כָּל טוֹבוֹת שְׁאָר הֶחֳדָשִׁים וּזְמַנִּים, אֲבָל לֹא כָּל כָּךְ כְּחֹדֶשׁ אָב שֶׁהוּא אָב אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת אֲפִילּוּ מֵחֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב, וְזֶהוּ הַסִּימָן א"ת ב"ש פֶּסַח תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב, שֶׁלֶּעָתִיד יִהְיוּ כָּל הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת בְּטֵלִין חוּץ מִתִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת וְאָב לְכֻלָּם, גַּם מוֹעֵד שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב שֶׁהוּא לְעֵת עַתָּה הָאָב יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן נִכְלָל בְּמוֹעֵד חֹדֶשׁ הָאָב, וְזֶה "לְמוֹעֵד חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב".


*“You shall keep the festival of matsot in the time of the month of Aviv, seven days shall you eat matsot as I command you, for in the month of Aviv you came out of Egypt.”* (Shemot, 34:18) *Aviv* is related to the word *Av*, “father,” which includes all the generations, meaning all the good of all the other months and seasons, but not as much as in the month of Aviv itself, which is the father, which has in it even all the good of the month of Aviv. And this is why if you exchange the letters of Pesach through the *atbash* system⁸⁹ with *tav, bet* with *shin* (hence, *atbash*), *gimel* with *reish, dalet* with *koof*, and so forth. you arrive at the initial letters of Tisha B’Av, for in the future all the festivals will be nullified except for Tisha B’Av (which will be transformed into the ultimate festival), which contains all the festivals and is the father of them all. Also, the time of the month of Av that is now the father (first of the months), will also be in the time of the month of Av, and this is the meaning of “the time of the month of Aviv.”

**כָּל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לִי.** הַיְינוּ שֶׁאִם תִּרְאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ צַעַר וְדַאֲגַת פַּרְנָסָה לְהַצַּדִּיק וּתְהֵא לְךָ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם תַּרְעוֹמוֹת עַל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל זֶה אָמַר "כָּל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לִי", כִּי כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּפְטָר פֶּטֶר שֶׁל רַחְמָנוּת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִי, כִּי אֲנִי נִקְרָא אָב הָרַחֲמָן, רַק שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה מֵבִין כַּוָּונָתִי וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן "וְלֹא יֵרָאוּ פָנַי רֵיקָם" הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּתָּנָה מוּעֶטֶת מְחוּיָּב אַתָּה לִיתֵּן לְכָל עָנִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אַף שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁאֵין אֲנִי מְרַחֵם עָלָיו, וְאַף דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שבת קנ"א:) גְּמוּרֵי דְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם אַהֲדוֹרֵי אַפִּתְחָא לָא מְהַדַּר, וּמִדִּמְהַדַּר מוּכָח שֶׁאֵינוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אַף עַל פִּי כֵן חַיָּיב אַתָּה לִיתֵּן לוֹ דָּבָר מוּעָט כְּדֵי חִיּוּתוֹ.


*“All that opens the womb is Mine, and every firstborn among your cattle, whether ox or sheep.”* (Shemot, 34:20)
If you see that the *Tsaddik* suffers and worries over making a living, you may, God forbid, bring accusations against God concerning this. This is why it says, “all that opens the womb is Mine,”⁹⁰) is closely related to the word “compassion” (*rachem*). every time an opening of compassion is opened it is only from Me, because I am called the Father of Compassion. It is only that you do not understand My intentions. Nevertheless, (as the following verse ends), “none shall appear before Me empty-handed,” meaning you are required to give at least a small gift to a poor man, even if you see that I am not compassionate with him. Even though we find in the Gemara (*Shabbat*, 151b), “Rabbi Yosef said: We assert that a scholar will not suffer poverty. But we see that he does suffer poverty. Even if he suffers poverty, he does not engage in begging,” yet if he is not a scholar and he must resort to begging, then you are required to give him something small to sustain his life.

**שְׁמָר לְךָ אֵת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם.** בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ נִמְצָא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁמִירוֹת וְאַזְהָרוֹת נֶגֶד מִסְפַּר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים, לְכָל שֵׁבֶט נְקוּדָּה וְאַזְהָרָה הַנִּצְרֶכֶת לוֹ.


*“Guard that which I command you today ….”* (Shemot, 34:11)
In this *Parsha* twelve kinds of guarding and warnings are mentioned corresponding to the twelve tribes, with each tribe having one essential point of guarding necessary for it.


###### Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Ki Tisa 13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Mei%20HaShiloach/s/Volume%20I,_Exodus,_Ki%20Tisa/r/13)


**וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה.** בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (במדבר רבה פרשה ד',ד') בִּשְׁבִיל חִיבָּתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁנִיתִי עֲלֵיהֶם, אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי "פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה" וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים שֶׂה, וְאוּמּוֹת נִקְרָאִים חֲמוֹר וּפָדִיתִי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאוּמּוֹת כוּ׳. הָעִנְיָן הוּא כְּמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִיזַ"ל שֶׁמִּי שֶׁמּוּרְגָּל לְדַבֵּר שֶׁקֶר תַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁאַף לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם לֹא יְדַבֵּר שֶׁקֶר, וְכֵן מִי שֶׁפָּגַם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּמַאֲכָלוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת גַּם בְּמַאַכְלֵי שַׁבָּת יְצַמְצֵם עַצְמוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁתּוּכַל לְצַמְצֵם הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן הַחֵטְא, וְכֵן הָיָה הָעִנְיָן בְּיָרָבְעָם שֶׁחָלַק עַל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ וְתָלָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַחֵטְא עַל שְׁלֹמֹה בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תִּיקּוּן לְיָרָבְעָם, וְזֶהוּ "וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה", וְיָרָבְעָם נִפְדָּה בְּמַה שֶּׁנִּרְשַׁם חֵטְא גַּם עַל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ.
